Surha Tal Bird Sanctuary 
 
2303. SHRI BABU SINGH KUSHWAHA: 
 
Will the Minister of ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE be pleased to 
state:  
 
(a) whether Surha Tal Bird Sanctuary, located in Ballia, Uttar Pradesh has been 
notified/designated as a wetland and if so, the details thereof; 
 
(b) the details of funds allocated by the Government for the conservation, development and 
management of the said sanctuary and the amount actually utilized therefrom during the last 
three years, item-wise; 
 
(c) the expenditure incurred on conservation, habitat improvement, biodiversity enhancement, 
wetland management, water management, protection of migratory birds and other related 
activities during the said period; 
 
(d) whether the Government has launched any special scheme, project or Central assistance 
programme for the conservation of Surna Tal Bird Sanctuary biodiversity enhancement, 
wetland conservation and management and promotion of eco-tourism; and 
 
(e) if so, the details and present status thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND 
CLIMATE CHANGE 
 (SHRI KIRTI VARDHAN SINGH) 
 
(a) to (e) The Jai Prakash Narayan Bird Sanctuary (Surha Tal Bird Sanctuary) has been 
designated as a Wetland of International Importance under Ramsar convention (Ramsar Site) 
in view of its ecological importance.  It is the 100th Ramsar site in the Country. The Ministry 
of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEF&CC), is currently implementing a 
Centrally Sponsored Scheme (CSS) namely, the National Plan for Conservation of Aquatic 
Ecosystems (NPCA) for conservation and management of wetlands in the country on cost 
sharing basis between Central Government and respective State Governments. The scheme 
provides funds for the Integrated Management Plans (IMPs)/Framework Management Plans 
(FMPs) received from the States/UTs, including Uttar Pradesh, for conservation and 
management of wetlands. It aims at holistic conservation and restoration of wetlands for 
achieving the desired water quality enhancement, besides improvement in biodiversity and 

2 
 
ecosystems through an integrated and multi-disciplinary approach. The State Wetland 
Authority of Uttar Pradesh functions as an apex body for integrated management of wetlands 
and submits proposals under the NPCA scheme for consideration of the Ministry. Further 
Ministry provides financial assistance to the States/UTs under CSS "Development of Wildlife 
Habitats" for conservation and management of protected areas, conservation of wildlife outside 
protected areas and recovery of critically endangered species and its habitats as per the Annual 
Plan of Operation received from the States/UTs, including state of Uttar Pradesh. The financial 
assistance to the State/UTs includes activities for the protection and management of wildlife 
like patrolling, habitat management, awareness programme, maintenance of fire lines, 
engagement of protection watchers, Eco development and support for activities related to   eco-
tourism. The details of funds released/utilized during last three financial years to Jai 
Prakash  Narayan (Surah Tal) Bird Sanctuary in Uttar Pradesh under the CSS-Development of 
Wildlife Habitats are as given in Annexure. 
 
MoEF&CC has taken several steps for protection and preservation of wetlands across 
the country, which include, implementation of Ramsar Convention on wetlands, Wetlands 
(Conservation and Management) Rules, 2017 under the provisions of the Environment 
(Protection) Act, 1986, a dedicated Wetlands Web Portal(https://indianwetlands.in), Mission 
Sahbhagita and Save Wetlands Campaign for peoples and stakeholders’ participation in the 
wetlands conservation and management, Amrit Dharohar initiative to promote unique 
conservation values of Ramsar sites. The four key components of Amrit Dharohar are Species 
and Habitat Conservation, Nature Tourism, Wetlands Livelihoods and Wetlands Carbon 
Assessment. The expected outcomes of the initiative include the safeguarding and enhancing 
biological diversity, carbon sequestration and ground water recharge being co benefit.

†2306. Shri Tariq Anwar: 
 
Will the Minister of YOUTH AFFAIRS AND SPORTS be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government has conducted a State/UT -wise assessment 
of the sports infrastructure, projects sanctioned, Khelo India State 
Centres of Excellence (KISCE), accredited academies and the 
assistance provided to athle tes under the Khelo India Scheme since the 
financial year 2023-24 to till date; 
 
(b) if so, the details thereof; 
 
(c) whether the Government has reviewed the ongoing programmes 
implemented for talent identification, training of athletes, sports science 
and sports medicine support and the effective utilization of sports 
infrastructure; 
 
(d) if so, the major findings/outcomes thereof; 
 
(e) whether the Government is considering for providing additional 
central assistance or sanctioning new projects under the K helo India 
Scheme for the development of sports infrastructure, training facilities, 
centres of excellence for talented athletes in Bihar, particularly in the 
Seemanchal region; and 
 
(f) if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF YOUTH AFFAIRS & SPORTS  
[ DR. MANSUKH MANDAVIYA ] 

Page 2 of 2 
 
(a) to (f) ‘Sports’ being a State subject, the responsibility for 
development of sports, including reviewing of ongoing programmes 
implemented for talent identification, training of athletes, sports science 
and sports medi cine support and the effective utilization of sports 
infrastructure, rests primarily with the respective State/Union Territory 
Governments. The Union Government supplements their efforts by 
bridging critical gaps through its schemes and programmes. The Khelo 
India Scheme is being implemented across the country, including in the 
State of Bihar, with the objective of strengthening sports infrastructure, 
identifying and nurturing sporting talent and providing structured 
training and other support to athletes. Under the Scheme, financial 
assistance is provided for development of sports infrastructure and 
support is extended through Khelo India State Centres of Excellence 
(KISCEs), Khelo India Centres (KICs), Khelo India Accredited Academies 
(KIAAs), Khelo India Athletes (KIAs) and other components of the 
Scheme. 
 
The Khelo India Scheme is a demand -driven scheme. Proposals received 
from State/UT Governments and other eligible entities are considered for 
financial support, subject to their completeness, technical f easibility, 
infrastructure gaps, sporting potential, readiness for implementation and 
availability of funds under the Scheme.  
 
The details of various sports facilities under the Khelo India Scheme, 
such as Sports Infrastructure, Khelo India Centres (KICs), Khelo India 
State Centres of Excellence (KISCEs) and Khelo India Accredited 
Academies (KIAAs) along with Khelo India Athletes (KIAs) and coaches, 
across the country, including in Seemanchal region of the State of Bihar, 
are available in the public domain  on the dashboard of the Ministry at 
https://dashboard.kheloindia.gov.in. 
 
The implementation of the Khelo India Scheme is continuously 
monitored through established review and monitoring mechanisms and 
regular interaction with State Governments, implementing agencies and 
other stakeholders. The Government has taken various measures to 
strengthen talent identification and development, including identification 
of sporting talent through Khelo India competitions and Talent 
Identification and Development initi atives, provision of structured 
training through Khelo India Centres, Khelo India State Centres of 
Excellence and Khelo India Accredited Academies, and support for 
coaching, sports science, sports medicine, nutrition and competition 
exposure, as per the extant Scheme guidelines.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF CULTURE 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2307 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 03.08.2026 
 
Gyan Bharatam Mission and Preservation of Manuscript Heritage 
 
2307. Smt. Himadri Singh: 
          Shri Bhartruhari Mahtab: 
          Smt. Shobhanaben Mahendrasinh Baraiya:  
          Shri Tanuj Punia:  
          Shri Manish Jaiswal: 
          Shri Satish Kumar Gautam:  
          Smt. Mala Rajya Laxmi Shah:  
          Shri Gopal Jee Thakur: 
          Shri Alok Sharma: 
          Shri Janardan Mishra:  
          Shri Jagdambika Pal: 
 
Will the Minister of CULTURE be pleased to state: 
(a) the details of main objective of the recently launched 'Gyan Bharatam Mission' along with funds 
allocated by the Government thereon; 
(b) the details of number of manuscripts and rare texts identified, documented and digitised under 
the said Mission, State/UT-wise, particularly in Bihar especially in Darbhanga region and 
district-wise in Madhya Pradesh, since its launch; 
(c) whether the Government has established any institutional mechanism to encourage participation 
of private custodians, religious institutions, libraries and universities in the preservation and 
digitisation of manuscripts; 
(d) if so, the details thereof; 
(e) the details of measures taken/being taken by the Government to promote scholarly access, 
research and public outreach of digitised manuscripts under the said Mission; and 
(f) whether the Government is considering for taking any special initiative to preserve Darbhanga's 
rich Mithila manuscript tradition, Sanskrit texts and historical documents? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF CULTURE AND TOURISM 
(SHRI GAJENDRA SINGH SHEKHAWAT) 
 
(a) & (b) Gyan Bharatam Mission (GBM), announced during Union Budget 2025-26, is an initiative of 
the Ministry of Culture (MoC), Government of India to undertake manuscripts related activities. The 
objectives of this initiative are as follows: 
I. To leverage advanced technology to significantly enhance the pace of digitization and 
documentation of manuscripts. 

II. Conducting survey and registration of manuscripts. 
III. To document and catalogue Indian manuscripts, wherever they may be, maintain accurate and 
up-to-date information about them and the conditions under which they may be conserved. 
IV. To facilitate usage of manuscripts and promote ready access to these manuscripts through 
publications, both in book form as well as machine readable form. 
V. To facilitate conservation and preservation of manuscripts through training awareness and 
financial support. 
VI. To boost scholarship and research in the study of Indian languages and manuscriptology. 
VII. To build up a National Digital Repository (NDR). 
 
To support the initiative, the Standing Finance Committee (SFC) has sanctioned Rs.491.66 crore for 
the period 2025-2031. National Manuscript Survey was launched in March, 2026 across all States and 
Union Territories (UTs) of the country to identify and document manuscript holdings, repositories and 
custodians representing diverse languages and scripts. During the survey, more than 1.19 crore 
manuscripts have been reported. The total number of digitized manuscripts available across the country 
is over 8 lakh, out of which, more than 4.40 lakh manuscripts are available on Gyan Bharatam portal at 
present for public access, in view mode which is accessible state-wise. 
 
(c) & (d)   The mission has established an institutional mechanism through Cluster Centres and 
Independent Centres which include universities, research institutions, libraries, archives, private 
custodians, religious institutions, and other stakeholders to undertake manuscript related activities. 
States / Union Territories (UTs) have also been engaged to act as Nodal Coordinating Authority for 
Gyan Bharatam implementation within the State / UT concerned. 
 
(e) Access to digitized copies of manuscript is facilitated in accordance with the rights of 
custodians and rights holders. Wherever permissible, manuscripts and associated metadata may be 
made available for public and scholarly research through the National Digital Repository, while 
sensitive, restricted or rights-protected materials may be subject to appropriate access conditions. 
 
(f)  GBM is a pan-India initiative aimed at preserving India’s manuscript heritage, irrespective of 
script, language, knowledge tradition, region, or the custodial traditions of communities. Institutions 
located in Bihar namely (i) Nava Nalanda Mahavihar, Nalanda (ii) Khuda Bakhsh Oriental Public 
Library, Patna and (iii) Shri Bodh Gaya Math, Bodh Gaya have onboarded with GBM to undertake 
manuscript related activities.

2308. SHRI VISHNU DAYAL RAM: 
  SHRI DUSHYANT SINGH: 
  SMT. BIJULI KALITA MEDHI: 
  SHRI ASHISH DUBEY:  
 
Will the Minister of YOUTH AFFAIRS AND SPORTS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government has made any progress in implementing the 
Khelo Bharat Niti 2025 across the Country and if so, the details thereof, 
State/UT-wise;  
(b) the details of mechanisms established to ensure effective coordination 
among Central Ministries, State Governments, National Sports Federations, 
educational institutions and other stakeholders;  
(c) the manner in which the Government is leveraging the Khelo Bh arat Niti 
to strengthen India’s preparations for the medal in Asian and Olympic Games 
and creating a sustainable pipeline of medal-winning athletes for the Country; 
and 
(d) the details of number of States and Union Territories that have adopted or 
are in the process of aligning or formulating, their sports policies in line with 
the vision and objectives of the Khelo Bharat Niti 2025, State/UT-wise? 
  

Page 2 of 2 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF YOUTH AFFAIRS AND SPORTS 
[DR MANSUKH MANDAVIYA] 
 
(a) to (c): Khelo Bharat Niti, 2025 provides a whole-of-Government framework 
for sports development through convergence among Central Ministries, 
National Sports Federations (NSFs), educational institutions, the private 
sector and other stakeholders. The policy is being implemented th rough the 
existing schemes of Department of Sports and Sports Authority of India in 
coordination with recognized NSFs. It provides a structured grassroots -to-
elite athlete development pathway with a view to improving India’s 
performance at the upcoming Olympics, Paralympics, and other international 
sporting events and supporting preparations for the 2036 Olympic Games. 
The policy focuses on early talent identification, coaching, sports science, 
sports medicine, quality infrastructure and enhanced competitio n exposure. 
Through schemes such as Khelo India, National Centres of Excellence 
(NCOEs), Target Olympic Podium Scheme (TOPS) and Assistance to National 
Sports Federations (ANSF), the Government is building a sustained pipeline 
of athletes across priority sporting disciplines.   
(d): The Khelo Bharat Niti 2025 strengthens talent identification, structured 
training, sports science/medicine support and funding mechanisms in States, 
building a broad -based athlete pipeline aimed at the 2036 Olympics. Sports 
policies of individual States and Union Territories have been assessed 
internally by this Department for alignment. Many of the States’ Sports 
Policies are substantially aligned, and this Department has encouraged other 
States for aligning their State policy in line with KBN 2025.

Will the Minister of LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT be pleased to 
state:  
 
(a)the details of total number of industrial accidents reported in the 
country during the last ten  years and the current year, along with 
the number of deaths and injuries caused therein, State/UT-wise; 
(b)the details of such accidents caused due to violations of safety 
protocols, non -compliance with statutory regulations, failure to 
provide safety equipment, negligence of the management,  human 
errors or any other connected reasons thereof; 
(c)the details of industries, contractors, establishments etc., held 
liable for such violations along with the actions taken against them 
by the Government, including imposition of fines,  suspension, 
cancellation of licenses, blacklisting etc.; 
(d)whether the Government has carried out any assessment to find 
out the reasons for recurring industrial accidents despite existing 
safety laws and if so, the findings thereof and if not,  the reasons 
therefor; and 
(e)whether the Government has proposed any measures t o reduce 
industrial accidents,  ensure safety of workers and stricter 
enforcement of safety measures in the industries across the  
country and if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT 
(SUSHRI SHOBHA KARANDLAJE) 
 
(a) to (e): The Central Government has enacted the Occupational 
Safety, Health and Working Conditions (OSH&WC) Code, 2020, which 
has come into force from 21.11.2025, to regulate occupational safety, 
health and working conditions of the persons  employed in an 
establishment including factories and for matters connected 
therewith or incidental thereto.  The Central Government has also 
notified OSH & WC (Central) Rules 2026 on 08.05.2026. 
Contd..2/- 

:: 2 :: 
  There are elaborate provisions pertaining to occupational 
safety, health, welfare, hazardous processes, penalties and 
procedures etc. under the OSH & WC Code 2020 and rules framed 
thereunder. The Occupier and Managers of the factories registered 
under the OSH & WC Code 2020 are required to comp ly with the 
provisions of the Code and rules framed thereunder. In case of 
violations of any of the provisions thereof, the Chief Inspector cum 
Facilitator / Inspector cum Facilitator, notified under the OSH & WC 
Code 2020, is empowered to initiate legal action against the occupier 
and manager of the factories. 
         Directorate General Occupational Safety and Health 
(DGOSH), an attached office of Ministry of Labour and Employment 
collects the data of accidental deaths and injuries of workers from 
States / Union Territories (UTs) in case of factories registered under

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
DEPARTMENT OF SCHOOL EDUCATION & LITERACY 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2310 
ANSWERED ON 03.08.2026 
 
Establishment of Navodaya Vidyalayas and Kendriya Vidyalayas in 
Rajnandgaon 
 
†2310. Shri Santosh Pandey:  
 
Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state:  
 
(a) whether the Government proposes to establish Navodaya Vidyalayas and 
Kendriya Vidyalayas in Mohla-Manpur-Ambagarh Chowki and Khairagarh-
Chhuikhadan-Gandhi districts of Rajnadgaon Lok Sabha Constituency of 
Chhattisgarh, if so, the details thereof;  
 
(b) whether land has been selected/acquired for the establishment of a Navodaya 
vidyalaya in Mohla-Manpur-Ambagarh Chowki district; and  
 
(c) if so, the details thereof along with the timeline fixed for the establishment of 
these schools? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(SHRI JAYANT CHAUDHARY) 
 
(a) to (c): The Navodaya Vidyalaya Scheme envisages for opening of one Navodaya 
Vidyalaya (NV) in each district of the country. Opening of new NVs in uncovered 
districts is a continuous process which depends on the willingness of the concerned 
State Government/UT administration to make available requisite suitable land, free 
of cost, for construction of the permanent building and making available required 
temporary building, free of rent, to run the Vidyalaya till the permanent building is 
constructed. Sanction and opening of new NVs depends on approval by the 
competent authority as per extant procedures. As per information received from 
Navodaya Vidyalaya Samiti (NVS), Mohla-Manpur-Ambagarh Chowki and 
Khairagarh-Chhuikhadan-Gandai districts of Chhattisgarh do not have NV at present. 
As on date, 27 districts of Chhattisgarh have been covered under the scheme and 28 
NVs are functional in these districts. 
Opening of new Kendriya Vidyalayas (KVs) is a continuous process. KVs are 
opened primarily to cater to the educational needs of the wards of transferable 
Central Government Employees including Defence & Para-military personnel, 

Central Autonomous Bodies, Central Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs) and Central 
Institute of Higher Learning (IHL) by providing a common programme of education 
throughout the country. Proposals for opening of new KVs may be sponsored by 
Ministries or Departments of the Government of India / State Governments / Union 
Territories (UTs) Administrations, with commitment to provide requisite resources 
including land and temporary accommodation for setting up a new KV as per norms. 
As on date, 40 KVs are functional in Chhattisgarh. As per information received from 
Kendriya Vidyalaya Sangathan (KVS), no feasible proposal for opening of new KV in 
Mohla-Manpur-Ambagarh Chowki and Khairagarh-Chhuikhadan-Gandai districts of 
Rajnadgaon Lok Sabha parliamentary constituency of Chhattisgarh has been 
received from the concerned State Government/district administration.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF TOURISM 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO.†2311 
 ANSWERED ON 03.08.2026 
 
DEVELOPMENT AND PROMOTION OF TOURISM IN BALLIA  
†2311. SHRI SANATAN PANDEY: 
     
Will the Minister of TOURISM be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government is aware of the fact that there is significant 
potential for religious and cultural tourism in the Ballia Lok Sabha 
Constituency to promote tourism infrastructure, tourist facilities and 
its publicity; 
(b) whether the Government has proposed or approved any project for 
the development of any religious or historical site in the Ballia region 
under the 'Pilgrimage Rejuvenation and  Spiritual, Heritage 
Augmentation Drive (PRASHAD) Scheme'; 
(c) if so, the details of approved wo rks, estimated cost and current 
progress under the said projects; and 
(d) whether the Government proposes to provide any additional scheme 
or financial  assistance to promote tourism infrastructure, tourist 
facilities and its publicity in the region? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF TOURISM          (SHRI GAJENDRA SINGH SHEKHAWAT) 
 
(a)to (d): Identification, d evelopment and promotion of tourism 
destinations and products is primarily undertaken by the concerned State 
Governments (SGs)/Union Territory Administrations (UTAs). However, the 
Ministry of Tourism through its central sector schemes of ‘Swadesh 
Darshan ( SD)’, ‘Swadesh Darshan 2.0 (SD2.0)’, ‘Challenge Based 
Destination Development (CBDD)’ – a sub scheme of SD2.0 and ‘Pilgrimage 
Rejuvenation and Spiritual, Heritage Augmentation Drive (PRASHAD)’ 
complements the efforts of tourism infrastructure development b y 
extending financial assistance to the State Governments/UT 
Administrations; subject to adherence to scheme guidelines, submission 
of Detailed Project Reports (DPRs), availability of funds, Government 
directions, inter-se priority etc. 

 
Currently, no proposal is under consideration for the development of 
any religious or historical site in the Ballia region under the PRASHAD 
Scheme. 
 
The Ministry under its Swadesh Darshan Scheme, has sanctioned a 
project namely ‘ Development of Bijnor -Meerut- Kanpur- Kanpur Dehat - 
Banda-Ghazipur- Salempur -Ghosi- Balia- Ambedkar Nagar - Aligarh-
Fatehpur- Deoria- Mahoba-   Sonbhadra- Chandauli-Mishrikh-Bhadohi’ at a 
cost of Rs. 67.51 Crore. 
 
Furthermore, t he Ministry of Tourism promotes the tourism 
destinations and products of the country in a holistic manner. The tourism 
destinations and products are showcased through the Incredible India 
Digital Platform (IIDP), which promotes these destinations and products 
through its official social media platforms on a regular basis.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2313 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 03.08.2026 
 
Increasing Deforestation 
 
2313. SHRI MANICKAM TAGORE B: 
 
Will the Minister of ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE be pleased to 
state: 
(a) whether Government is aware of increasing deforestation across the country, if so, the 
details thereof, along with the forest cover trends in recent years and the steps taken to 
prevent further degradation; 
(b) whether diversion of forest land for industrial and infrastructure projects has increased, if 
so, the details thereof and assessment of its impact on biodiversity and ecological 
balance; 
(c) whether compensatory afforestation programmes have effectively restored lost forest 
cover, if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons for failure and corrective measures 
taken; 
(d) whether illegal logging and encroachments continue to threaten forests, if so, the details 
thereof and enforcement actions taken to curb such activities; and  
(e) whether the Government has strengthened monitoring mechanisms using technology for 
forest conservation, if so, the details thereof and the outcomes achieved in preventing 
deforestation? 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND 
CLIMATE CHANGE  
(SHRI KIRTI VARDHAN SINGH) 
 
(a) to (e) There is an increasing trend in forest and tree cover in the country over the last 
decade. As per the India State of Forest Report (ISFR) 2023, the total forest and tree cover is 
8,27,357.95 sq km, which is 25.17% of the geographical area of the country. This represents 
an increase of 1,445.81 sq km over ISFR 2021. Further, between ISFR 2013 and ISFR 2023, 
India’s forest and tree cover registered a net increase of 37,378 sq km. 
 
Diversion of forest land is regulated under the Van (Sanrakshan Evam Samvardhan) 
Adhiniyam, 1980. During 01.04.2021 to 31.03.2026, approvals for diversion of 105594.32 
hectares of forest land were accorded after following the prescribed procedure and subject to 
mitigation measures such as compensatory afforestation and wildlife conservation 
safeguards. 
 
In compliance of the conditions stipulated under the Van (Sanrakshan Evam Samvardhan) 
Adhiniyam, 1980, the compensatory afforestation is taken up by the concerned State/UT. As 
per the reports received from the States/UTs, the compensatory afforestation over an area of 
1,78,261.52 hectares has been carried out during the last five years. The survival percentage 
of these plantations have been reported between 40% to 100%.  

 
In addition, Ministry provides technical and financial support to the States and Union 
Territories through various schemes and programmes of the Central Government for 
increasing forest and tree cover, including protection, conservation and sustainable 
management of forests in the country. These include, inter alia, the National Mission for a 
Green India (GIM), Nagar Van Yojana (NVY), Mangrove Initiative for Shoreline Habitats 
and Tangible Incomes (MISHTI), Compensatory Afforestation Fund Management and 
Planning Authority (CAMPA), Integrated Development of Wildlife Habitats, and forest 
fire prevention and management schemes. 
 
The Ministry issues advisories to States/UTs to protect forests and trees, and mitigation of 
deforestation as per the provisions of the law including prevention of illegal logging and 
encroachments. Measures taken include survey and demarcation of forest land, boundary 
pillars, regular patrolling, legal action under applicable laws and community participation 
through Joint Forest Management Committees.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
DEPARTMENT OF HIGHER EDUCATION 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO- 2314 
ANSWERED ON - 03/08/2026 
 
Employability of Graduates from UP 
 
2314.   Adv Priya Saroj:  
 Shri Pushpendra Saroj:  
 
Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state:  
(a) whether the Government has undertaken any study to evaluate whether reduced disciplinary 
specialization under the NEP undergraduate curriculum has affected the employability and 
higher education preparedness of graduates from Uttar P radesh (UP), if so, the details 
thereof; 
(b) the placement rates and postgraduate admission rates of undergraduate students in Central 
Universities of UP during the three years preceding and following implementation of the 
revised curriculum; 
(c) whether employers, professional bodies or academic experts have raised concerns 
regarding declining subject proficiency among graduates; and 
(d) if so, the action taken by the Government in this regard? 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(DR. SUKANTA MAJUMDAR) 
 
(a) to (d): Government of India has framed the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 which 
emphasises on multidisciplinary flexible curricular structures, integration of skills and 
recommends that the pedagogy must evolve to make education more experiential, inquiry -
driven, discovery-oriented, and learner-centred. It also aims to increase the employabilit y of 
students by providing them with opportunities for internships with local industry, businesses, 
artists, crafts persons etc. 
In line with the vision of NEP 2020, the Government has issued key guidelines and  has taken 
several initiatives to upgrade curr icula, pedagogy, in order to create future -ready talent 
pipeline. 

To upgrade the higher education curricula, the All -India Council for Technical Education 
(AICTE) has revised its Model Curricula with inputs from industry experts by integrating 
Artificial Intelligence (AI), Data Science (DS), Machine Learning (ML), Cyber Security, 
Robotics, Quantum Computing, and other emerging technologies across technical disciplines. 
AICTE also undertakes regular consultations with industry, professional bodies, academia, and 
other stakeholders to ensure that technical education remains  relevant, competency -based, 
multidisciplinary, and aligned with evolving workforce requirements keeping in line with the 
objectives of NEP.  
AICTE’s Approval Process Handbook 2024 -25 to 2026 -27 has “Essential and Desirable 
Requirements for Technical Institutions”, which include Institute-Industry Cell, establishment 
of Institution ’s Innovation Council and compulsory internship for final year students as 
essential requirements for approval. 
To enhance employability of the students and achieve the objectives of NEP 2020, the National 
Credit Framework (NCrF) has been issued, enabling integration of skill education into 
academia. The NCrF has a provision for the accumulation of a maximum of 50% of the total 
credit required through skill-based courses. 
Further, the University Grants Commission has issued “Guidelines on Sustainable and Vibrant 
University-Industry Linkage System for Indian Universities ” to promote Research & 
Development and develop the skill sets amongst the learners and make them industry ready.  
 
 UGC has also introduced “Guidelines for Internship/Research Internship for Under Graduate 
Students”, with an aim to improve employability, develop interest for research and provide 
exposure to emerging technologies. Further, UGC has also formulated the “UGC Guidelines 
for Higher Educational Institutions to Offer Apprenticeship Embedded Degree Programme 
(AEDP)” to embed the competencies required by the industry in the university curriculum. 
 
The Ministry of Education implements the National Apprenticeship Training Scheme (NATS) 
to impart on -the-job training in collaboration with industry to enhance the employability of 
youth and has also launched SWAYAM Plus platform in February 2024. This platform offers 
more than 500 employability -focused courses. These courses have been curated from more 
than 80 industry partners across 15 sectors, including Information Technology, Artificial 
Intelligence, Semiconductor Manufacturing, BFSI, Healthcare, a nd Advanced Manufacturing 
etc. More than 06 lakh learners have enrolled on SWAYAM Plus platform for their Skill 
augmentation. 

 
Ministry of Education has impl emented the National Mission on Education through ICT 
(NMEICT) in alignment with NEP 2020. Under NMEICT, an enterprise resource planning 
(ERP) software platform SAMARTH has been launched , which aims to enable end -to-end 
digital transformation of administrative, academic, and governance processes in higher 
education institutions (HEIs). It is intended to streamline operations, reduce paperwork , 
enhance transparency, and improve service delivery for students, faculty and administrators of 
HEIs. Samarth has more than 40 modules including Admissions, Training & Placement. 
As per the report available on SAMARTH portal more than 17 lakh students have enrolled in 
Post Graduate programs including more than 26,000 enrolments in Central Universities in Uttar 
Pradesh that have adopted SAMARTH module, over the last three years. 
SAMARTH provides Training and Placement Module  in order  to streamline and automate 
campus recruitment, placement, and internship processes for HEIs. It simplifies company 
registration, job postings, centralises student pr ofile management, and provides access to job 
opportunity and internship. 28 Central Universities including from Uttar Pradesh have 
onboarded the Training and Placement Module, to provide job opportunities and to facilitate 
placement for students. 
Further, the placement of students depends upon several factors, including prevailing market 
conditions, students' preference to pursue higher education & research pathways and a growing 
interest in entrepreneurship and start-ups. Many undergraduate students also opt out of campus 
placements to appear in interviews on their own outside the campus or prepare for competitive 
examinations.  
According to the PLFS reports, the estimated Unemployment Rate (UR), on  usual status for 
persons of age 15 years and above has decreased from 6.1% in 2017 to 3.1% in 2025. Periodic 
Labour Force Survey (PLFS) reports, may be seen at: 
https://www.mospi.gov.in/uploads/publications_reports/publications_reports1780040415321_
0624fb13-fb47-40bc-b470-7c7e9635c3ef_PLFS_2025_F_REV_29052026.pdf

SHRI KANWAR SINGH TANWAR: 
 
Will the Minister of TOURISM be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the details of the steps taken to strengthen the global 
competitiveness of India's tourism sector through digital platforms, 
destination branding and international marketing campaigns thereof 
along with included destinations of Madhya Pradesh, particularly  

Dewas–Shajapur Lok Sabha Constituency and Himachal Pradesh, 
especially the Shimla Lok Sabha Constituency; 
(b) whether any digital ecosystem has been developed to integrate 
tourist services, destination information, bookings and grievance 
redressal through a unified platform and, if so, the details thereof, 
especially in Palghar in Maharashtra for Coastal tourism development 
and Himachal Pradesh along with registered destinations, users and 
services under it; 
(c) whether the Government has formulated any strategy to promote 
niche tourism segments, including wedding tourism, wellness 
tourism, cruise tourism, coastal tourism, rural tourism and spiritual 
tourism across the country; 
(d) if so, the details thereof, State/UT -wise, particularly for Madhya 
Pradesh, Rajasthan especially Bharatpur Lok Sabha Constituency and 
approved projects, financial assistance, number of tourists and 
employment generation district-wise in Himachal Pradesh, especially 
the Shimla Lok Sabha Constituency; 
(e) the details along with the measures taken to improve international 
tourist arrivals, average tourist expenditure and the contribution of 
tourism to employment and economic growth to GDP along with 
assessment of impact of the said initiatives thereof, parti cularly in 
Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra, including Jalgaon Lok Sabha 
Constituency and Palghar for Coastal tourism development during the 
last three years; 
(f) whether the Government proposes to promote tourism infrastructure 
and digitally integrated tourist destinations in Jalgaon Lok Sabha 
Constituency and if so, the details thereof; and  
(g) whether the Government proposes financial or infrastructure support 
for developing tourism circuits and heritage destinations in Dewas –
Shajapur? 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF TOURISM           (SHRI GAJENDRA SINGH SHEKHAWAT) 
 
(a) to (g): The Ministry of Tourism promotes tourism destinations and 
experiences across the country, including those in Madhya Pradesh, 
Himachal Pradesh, Maharashtra and Rajasthan, through a range of 
domestic and international promotional initiatives aimed at enhancing the 
global competitiveness of India's tourism sector. These initiatives include 

participation in international travel fairs and exhibitions, roadshows, 
integrated marketing campaigns, and digital and social media outreach. 
The Ministry has developed the Incredible India Digital Platform (IIDP) 
as a unified digital platform providing destination information, multilingual 
content, curated itineraries and integration with booking services for 
flights, hotels, cabs, buses and AS I monument tickets through partner 
platforms across the country. 
The Ministry has formulated National Strategies for Sustainable 
Tourism, Rural Tourism, Rural Homestays, MICE Tourism, Adventure 
Tourism, Medical & Wellness Tourism and Eco-tourism and circulated them 
to all State Governments and UT Administrations for imp lementation. The 
Ministry also promotes niche tourism segments, including wedding, 
wellness, cruise, coastal, rural and spiritual tourism, through its domestic 
and international promotional initiatives.  
Identification and development of tourism destinations is primarily 
the responsibility of the concerned State Governments/UT Administrations. 
The Ministry complements these efforts by providing financial assistance 
under the Swadesh Darshan, Swadesh Darsha n 2.0, Challenge Based 
Destination Development (CBDD) and SASCI schemes, subject to scheme 
guidelines. The details of projects sanctioned in Madhya Pradesh, 
Rajasthan, Maharashtra and Himachal Pradesh are enclosed at Annexure. 
The Ministry does not maintain constituency -wise data of 
international tourist arrivals, tourist expenditure, contribution of tourism 
to GDP and employment.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF SKILL DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2316 
ANSWERED ON 03.08.2026 
  
SKILL DEVELOPMENT FOR HEALTHCARE PROFESSIONALS  
 
2316. SHRI RAJMOHAN UNNITHAN:  
 
 Will the Minister of SKILL DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP be pleased 
to state: 
 
(a)  whether the Government has introduced specialised skill programmes for nurses, 
paramedics and allied healthcare professionals and if so, the details thereof;  
 
(b)  the total number of candidates trained under such programmes during the last three 
years and the current year;  
 
(c)  whether Kerala has been covered under these initiatives; and  
 
(d)  if so, the details of the steps taken/being taken by the Government to facilitate 
overseas employment of such trained healthcare professionals?  
  
 
ANSWER 
  
THE MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) IN THE MINISTRY OF SKILL 
DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP 
  
(SHRI JAYANT CHAUDHARY) 
  
(a) to (c) :  Under the Government of India’s Skill India Mission (SIM) , the Ministry of Skill 
Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE) delivers skill, re-skill and up-skill training through 
an extensive network of skill development centres  under various schemes, viz. Pradhan 
Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY), Jan Shikshan Sansthan (JSS), National 
Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme (NAPS) and Craftsman Training Scheme (CTS) through 
Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs), to all the sections of the society across the country 
including Kerala. The SIM aims at enabling youth of India to get future ready and equipped 
with industry relevant skills including in paramedical and allied healthcare sectors. 
 
PMKVY: Under the PMKVY, the Ministry supports training in job roles relevant to healthcare 
services. The major healthcare job roles under PMKVY 4.0 include Emergency Medical 
Technician-Basic, General Duty Assistant, Geriatric Caregiver (Institutional & Home Care), 
Healthcare Hygiene and Housekeeping Aide, Assistant Yoga Instructor, Panchakarma 
Assistant and Genetic Counselor. 
 
MSDE has launched the Training Programme  for Multi-Skilled Caregivers under PMKVY, in 
line with the Union Budget 2026 –27 announcements to skill 1.5 lakh caregiving professionals 
(1.3 lakh through MSDE ecosystem), creating a professionally trained workforce for 
healthcare, geriatric and home -based care while opening new employment opportunities, 
particularly for women and youth. 
 
NAPS: Under NAPS, apprenticeship opportunities are available across healthcare, 
paramedical, and allied healthcare sectors, based on the skill requirements of participating 
establishments. 
 

JSS: Under JSS Scheme, various healthcare -related skill development programmes are 
being implemented to enhance employability and livelihood opportunities, particularly for non-
literate, neo-literate, school dropouts, etc.   The healthcare-related courses offered under the 
JSS Scheme include Basic Health and Wellness Skills (Secondary School), Basic Health and 
Wellness Skills (Senior Secondary School), Fundamentals of POSHAK (Poshan Shiksha and 
Kaushal) for Anganwadi Karya Karta, Foundation Course in Healthcare, Front Line Health 
Worker, General Duty Assistant (GDA), Helpers for Hospitals and Nursing Homes, General 
Duty Attendant (GDA), Geriatric Assistant, and Optician. 
 
CTS: Under CTS, the Healthcare Sector trades being offered through Industrial Training 
Institutes (ITIs) include Dental Laboratory Equipment Technician, Geriatric (old age) Care, 
Health Sanitary Inspector, Physiotherapy Technician, Radiology Technician, etc. 
 
Coverage: Total number of candidates trained under the major skill development schemes of 
MSDE in paramedical and allied healthcare sectors since 2023 -24 up to 30 th June 2026 are 
as under:

Programme under Ministry of Health & Family Welfare: As per Ministry of Health & Family 
Welfare one-year Post Basic Diploma programmes in various clinical specialties have been 
developed in the Residency Mode (Earn While You Learn) by the Indian Nursing Council 
(INC), to strengthen the clinical competencies of registered nurses and to address the 
growing demand for specialized nursing care. These programmes provide structured, 
competency-based clinical training while enabling nurses to continue working during the 
course. 
 
(d):  MSDE has established and operationalized seven Skill India International Centres 
(SIICs) in different states on a pilot basis to facilitate international employment opportunities 
for the Indian youth. Further, MSDE, through the National Skill Development Corporation 
(NSDC), is facilitating overseas employment opportunities for healthcare professionals 
through country -specific workforce mobility initiatives. These initiatives include candidate 
mobilisation, language and domain -specific preparation, assessment and selection 
processes, employer engagement and deployment support in accordance with destination -
country requirements. Under these initiatives, healthcare professionals have been trained for 
overseas opportunities through programmes such as the Japan Technical Intern Training 
Programme (TITP) for Caregivers and the Israel Government -to-Government (G2G) 
Caregiver Programme.

UNSTARRED QUESTION No. 2317 
ANSWERED ON MONDAY, 3 AUGUST, 2026 / SHRAVANA 12, 1948 (SAKA) 
 
Bank Mitra Network in Tamil Nadu 
 
2317. DR. RANI SRIKUMAR: 
          SHRI C N ANNADURAI: 
          SHRI SELVAM G: 
 
Will the Minister of FINANCE be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether Government has undertaken any assessment of the functioning and effectiveness of the 
Bank Mitra network in Tamil Nadu in promoting financial inclusion and ensuring access to banking 
services in rural, tribal, coastal and underserved areas, if so, the details thereof; 
 
(b) the number of Bank Mitras presently engaged in Tamil Nadu, along with the number of villages 
covered, banking transactions facilitated and beneficiaries served during the last three years and the 
current year, year-wise and district-wise; 
 
(c) whether the Government has identified any shortage of Bank Mitras or gaps in banking outreach in 
aspirational, remote and economically weaker districts of Tamil Nadu, particularly in unbanked and 
underbanked Gram Panchayats, if so, the details thereof and the corrective measures taken in this 
regard; and 
 
(d) the steps take n to strengthen the Bank Mitra network in Tamil Nadu through additional 
deployments, enhanced remuneration, improved digital connectivity, doorstep banking facilities 
and capacity-building programmes? 
 
 ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE 
(SHRI PANKAJ CHAUDHARY) 
 
(a) & (b) As per data available on Jan Dhan Darshak (JDD) app, a total of 34,586 Business 
Correspondents (BCs) is presently engaged in Tamil Nadu as on 30.06.2026 and all 15,425 inhabited 
mapped villages in Tamil Nadu have been covered by Branch/BC/IPPB Centre within radius of 5 kms. 
The data related to banking transactions facilitated and beneficiaries served is not maintained centrally. 
Banks are ensuring the availability of  banking services in all areas including  rural, tribal, coastal and 
underserved areas. The number of BCs and their functioning and effectiveness are reviewed and 
monitored at regular intervals through the State Level Bankers' Committee (SLBC), District 
Consultative Committee (DCC), District Level Review Committee (DLRC) meetings to ensure 
adequate banking access.   
 
(c) Banks deploy BCs based on the business potential, population and geographical requirements to 
ensure adequate banking access. The Government, in coordination with banks through the State Level 
Bankers' Committee (SLBC), continuously monitors banking outreach. As per data available on JDD 
app, a total of 1702 BCs have been working in aspirational districts in Tamil Nadu and all 15,425 
inhabited mapped villages in Tamil Nadu have been covered by Branch/BC/IPPB Centre within radius 
of 5 kms.  
 
(d) Banks formulate a policy for engaging BCs with the approval of their Board of Directors’ wherein 
the banks pay reasonable commission/fee/incentives to the BCs, the rate and quantum of which is 
reviewed periodically. BCs undertake various banking activities such as opening bank accounts, 
completing Re-KYC, providing doorstep banking services including cash deposits and withdrawals, 
Direct Benefit Transfer Payments, enrolment under social security schemes and other basi c banking 
services particularly in rural and underserved areas. Banks impart quality and basic induction training 
to BC through Corporate BCs, covering device application usage and general banking besides regular 
training and capacity building programmes f or BCs to enhance their operational efficiency and 
customer service.

TO BE ANSWERED ON 03.08.2026 
STATUS OF PM-SYM IN TAMIL NADU 
 
2318. DR. KALANIDHI VEERASWAMY: 
 
Will the Minister of LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT be pleased to 
state:  
 
(a)the details of total number of workers enrolled under the Pradhan 
Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PM-SYM) scheme since its launch and 
the number of active subscribers as of the latest  date within Tamil 
Nadu; 
(b)the details of total contributions collected and the total pensions 
disbursed under the said scheme in the State; 
(c) the details of percentage of beneficiaries from rural, unorganized and 
marginalized communities along with the measu res taken by the 
Government to ensure that women workers are adequately covered; 
(d)the reasons for accounts becoming inactive or lapsing and the steps 
taken by the Government to improve retention and participation in the 
said scheme; 
(e)the details of pro gress in linking PM -SYM beneficiaries with other 
social security schemes and welfare initiatives; 
(f)the details of financial literacy and awareness programmes conducted 
by the Government  to educate workers about PM -SYM and their 
effectiveness in increasing enrollments; and 
(g)any new initiatives or policy measures planned by the Government to 
enhance coverage, benefits and accessibility of the PM -SYM scheme 
in the coming financial year? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT 
(SUSHRI SHOBHA KARANDLAJE) 
(a) to (g): Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maandhan (PM -SYM): PM -SYM 
scheme was launched in February, 2019 in order to provide old age 
protection to the workers of unorganised sector. This is a voluntary and 
contributory pension scheme. Under the scheme, a monthly assured 
pension of Rs. 3000/- is provided to the unorganised workers 
Contd..2/- 
 

:: 2 :: 
after attaining the age of 60 years. The workers in the age group of 18 to 
40 years whose monthly income is Rs. 15000/- or less and not a member 
of EPFO/ESIC/NPS (Contributed by Central Govt.) or not an income tax 
assessee are eligible to join the scheme. The monthly contribution 
amount ranges from Rs. 55/ - to Rs. 200/-, depending upon the entry age 
of the beneficiary. Under the schem e, 50% monthly contribution is 
payable by the beneficiary and equal matching contribution is paid by 
the Central Government. Enrolment in the Scheme is done through the 
Common Service Centres, with its network of about 4 lakh Centres 
across the country. El igible unorganised workers can also self -enrol 
through visiting the portal www.maandhan.in. 
  As on 29.07.2026, more than 54 lakh beneficiaries have been 
enrolled under PM-SYM scheme across the country. The participation of 
women unorganised workers in this scheme is 53.1%. 
  The 50 percent matching contribution of the Government 
under the PM -SYM Scheme across the country is Rs. 2,011.01 crore. 
Further, pension to the beneficiaries will start after attaini ng the age of 
60 years. Since the scheme was launched in February, 2019, the 
disbursement of pension will start not before February, 2039. 
  Under the PM-SYM Scheme, subscriber accounts may become 
inactive primarily due to non -payment of the prescribed mon thly 
contribution, which may occur on account of insufficient balance in the 
subscriber's bank account, change or closure of the linked bank account, 
or lack of continued awareness regarding regular contributions. 
  The steps taken by the Government to imp rove retention, 
increase participation and increase awareness are as under: 
(i) Holding periodic review meetings with States/UTs. 
(ii) Providing incentives to Common Services Centres (CSCs) for 
enrolling eligible beneficiaries under PM-SYM scheme. 
(iii) Launch of new features such as Voluntary Exit, Revival Module, 
Claim Status and Account Statement. 
(iv) Extension of the revival period of dormant accounts from one year 
to three years. 
(v) Two-way integration of PM-SYM with eShram portal. 
(vi) Conducting SMS campaigns for awareness generation. 
(vii) Addressing Chief Secretaries of States/UTs regarding enrolment 
under the PM-SYM Scheme. 
(viii) Organize nationwide special registration drive for enrolment of 
unorganised workers under the scheme.

Relaxations to Farmer Producer Companies  under the Companies Act, 
2013. 
1. Exemption from Minimum Capital Requirements: There is no mandatory 
statutory minimum paid -up capital threshold required at the time of 
incorporation. 
2. Immunity from Hostile Takeovers: Transfer of shares is strictly 
restricted to active primary producers or via board approval, ensuring the 
corporate structure remains member-controlled. 
3. Deviation from Capital-Based Voting Rights: Section 378D explicitly 
mandates a democratic voting structure ("one member, one vote"), 
exempting the company from rules where voting power is proportional to 
equity shareholding. 
4. No Ceiling on Membership: Unlike private limited companies, there is 
no maximum limit on the number of members a Farmer Producer Company 
can admit.

(a) the details of Khelo India projects, sports infrastructure, Khelo India 
Centres, training centres and athlete development initiatives sanctioned 
in Maharashtra during the last five years  and the current year, district -
wise; 
 
(b) the details of number of accredited academies, athletes and coaches 
supported under the  programme in the State, along with the financial 
assistance sanctioned, released and utilised; 
 
(c) whether the Government has assessed the challenges in 
implementing Khelo India in Maharashtra, including shortage of qualified 
coaches, inadequate sports infrastructure, delays in  release of funds , 
limited access to sports science, nutrition and sports medicine facilities 
and low  participation from rural, tribal and aspirational districts and if 
so, the details thereof; 
 
(d) the details of corrective measures taken by the Government to 
strengthen talent  identification, quality coaching and competitive 
opportunities for young athletes in the State; and 
 
(e) whether additional Khelo India Centres, infrastructure upgrades and 
equitable funding are  proposed for underserved districts in Maharashtra 
and if so, the details thereof? 
 

Page 2 of 3 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF YOUTH AFFAIRS & SPORTS  
[ DR. MANSUKH MANDAVIYA ] 
 
(a) to ( e) ‘Sports’ being a State subject, the responsibility for 
development of sports, including development of sports infrastructure 
and training facilities, academies, athletes and coaches, identification 
and nurturing of sporting talent, provision of competitive opportunities, 
and addressing the requirements of sports science, nutrition and sports 
medicine, rests primarily with the respective State/Uni on Territory 
Governments. The Union Government supplements their efforts by 
bridging critical gaps.  The Khelo India Scheme is being implemented 
across the country, including in the State of Maharashtra, with the 
objective of strengthening sports infrastructure, identifying and 
nurturing sporting talent and providing structured training and 
competition opportunities to athletes.  Under the Scheme, support is

of Excellence (KISCEs), Khelo I ndia Accredited Academies (KIAAs), 
Khelo India Athletes (KIAs) and other components of the Scheme.  The

the State of Maharashtra, are available in the public domain on the 
Ministry’s dashboards at https://dashboard.kheloindia.gov.in.

monitored through established review and monitoring mechanisms and 
regular interaction with State Governments, implementing agencies and 
other stakeholders.  The Government has taken various measures to 
strengthen talent identification and development, including identification 
of sporting talent through Khelo India competitions and Talent 
Identification and Development initiatives, provision of structured 
training through Khelo India Centres, Khelo India State Centres of 
Excellence and Khelo India Accredited Acade mies, and support for 
coaching, sports science, sports medicine, nutrition and competition 
exposure, as per the extant Scheme guidelines. 
 
The Government continues to strengthen the Khelo India initiative 
through its existing components, with emphasis on grassroots sports 
development, identification and nurturing of sporting talent and 
providing structured training and support to athletes. The Khelo India 
Scheme is a demand -driven scheme. Proposals received from the

their completeness, technical feasibility, infrastructure gaps, sporting

WELFARE OF WORKERS OF UNORGANIZED SECTORS 
 
2324. SHRI ANIL YESHWANT DESAI: 
 
Will the Minister of LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT be pleased to 
state:  
 
(a)whether it is a fact that there are several centrally monitored 
social security schemes are  being implemented in the country, if 
so, the details thereof, State/UT-wise; 
(b)the details of number of unorganised and gig workers registered 
under central social -security schemes in the country, particularly 
in Maharashtra; 
(c)the details of criteria or method of their recruitment and the 
number of workers who have  been extended benefits like 
insurance, pension, health, etc. under the said schemes during the 
last three years and the current year, State/UT and year-wise; and 
(d)the details of steps being taken by the Government to increase 
coverage and awareness of getting social security benefits among 
workers in informal sectors? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT 
(SUSHRI SHOBHA KARANDLAJE) 
 
(a) to (d): The Government is implementing various Central sector 
Social Security Schemes for providing social security benefits to 
different categories of workers across the country. These include, 
inter alia: 
(i) Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maandhan (PM-SYM): PM-SYM scheme 
was launched in February, 2019 in order to provide old age protection 
to the workers of unorganised sector. This is a voluntary and 
contributory pension scheme. Under the scheme, a monthly assured 
pension of Rs. 3000/ - is provided to the unorganised  workers after 
attaining the age of 60 years. The workers in the age group of 18 to 
40 years  whose  monthly  income is Rs. 15000/- or  less  and  not  a  
Contd..2/- 

:: 2 :: 
member of EPFO/ESIC/NPS (Contributed by Central Govt.) or not an 
income tax assess ee are eligible to join the scheme. The monthly 
contribution amount ranges from Rs. 55/- to Rs. 200/-, depending upon 
the entry age of the beneficiary. Under the scheme, 50% monthly 
contribution is payable by the beneficiary and equal matching 
contribution is paid by the Central Government. Enrolment in the 
Scheme is done through the Common Service Centres, with its 
network of about 4 lakh Centres across the country. Eligible 
unorganised workers can also self -enrol through visiting the 
portal www.maandhan.in. 
As on 29.07.2026, more than 54 lakh beneficiaries have been enrolled 
under PM-SYM scheme across the country, including more than 6.32 
lakh beneficiaries in the State of Maharashtra. 
 (ii) Ayushman Bhar at–Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB -
PMJAY): AB -PMJAY is a health assurance scheme that provides 
cashless secondary and tertiary healthcare coverage of up to Rs. 5 
lakh per family per year to eligible beneficiary families. It covers 
hospitalization expenses at empanelled public and private hospitals 
across the country.  
(iii) Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana (PMJJBY): PMJJBY is 
a life insurance scheme available to individuals aged 18 –50 years 
having a savings bank or post office account. It provid es life 
insurance coverage of Rs.2 lakh in the event of death due to any 
cause. Beneficiaries are required to pay an annual premium 
(currentlyRs.436 per annum), which is auto -debited from their bank 
account. 
(iv) Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana (PMSBY) : PMSBY is an 
accident insurance scheme available to persons aged 18 –70 years 
with a bank or post office account. It provides Rs.2 lakh for 
accidental death or total permanent disability and Rs.1 lakh for 
partial permanent disability. Beneficiaries are req uired to pay a 
nominal annual premium (currently Rs.20 per annum). 
(v) Labour Welfare Scheme and Health Care Facilities for Beedi, Cine 
and Non-Coal Mine Workers: The Labour Welfare Organisation under 
the Ministry of Labour & Employment provides healthcare and welfare 
services to Beedi, Cine and Non -Coal Mine workers through 
dispensaries, hospitals, diagnostic services and reimbursement of 
treatment expenses.  
Contd..3/- 

:: 3 :: 
(vi) Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana – Urban (PMAY-U): PMAY-U aims to 
provide pucca houses with basic civic amenities to eligible urban 
households through various implementation verticals.  
(vii) Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana – Gramin (PMAY -G): PMAY -G 
provides financial assistance for construction of pucca houses with 
basic amenities to elig ible rural households. Assistance is provided 
by the Central and State Governments, along with convergence with 
other schemes for sanitation, electricity, drinking water, etc.  
(viii) Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana – National Rural Livelihoods 
Mission (DAY -NRLM): DAY -NRLM mobilises poor rural households, 
especially women, into Self-Help Groups (SHGs) to promote financial 
inclusion, skill development and sustainable livelihoods. The Mission 
facilitates access to credit and capacity building through 
institutional support.  
(ix) Prime Minister Street Vendor's AtmaNirbhar Nidhi (PM SVANidhi): 
PM SVANidhi provides collateral-free working capital loans to eligible 
street vendors to support their livelihoods. The scheme offers 
interest subsidy on timely repayment and i ncentives for digital 
transactions.  
(x) Viksit Bharat – Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission 
(Gramin) [VB -G RAM (G)]: VB -G RAM (G) aims to strengthen rural 
livelihoods by providing up to 125 days of guaranteed employment 
annually to eligible rural ho useholds through labour -intensive 
developmental works.  
  The steps being taken by the Government to increase 
coverage and awareness of getting social security benefits among 
workers in informal sectors are as: 
(i) Holding periodic review meeting with States/ UTs.  
(ii) SMS campaign to create awareness.  
(iii) Addressing Chief Secretaries of States/UTs regarding enrolment 
under various schemes. 
(iv) Organise nationwide special registration drives. 
(v) To strengthen outreach, the Ministry leverages social media 
channels to disseminate videos, tutorials, and other informative 
content, making the initiative more accessible and engaging.

2325. SHRI KAMAKHYA PRASAD TASA: 
 
Will the Minister of ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether it is a fact that the civic agencies of Delhi have failed to control the terror of monkeys 
in different parts of Delhi, particularly in North Avenue, South Avenue and their adjacent 
Government offices, if so, the details thereof and the reasons for the same; 
(b) whether the Government is aware that monkey troops frequently barge into homes, snatch 
food from kitchens, destroy satellite dishes and damage outdoor fixtures, telephone wires, 
etc, if so, the details thereof; 
(c) whether the Government has provided funds for a pilot project on immune-contraception for 
controlling the population of monkeys; 
(d) if so, the details of funds provided to the States by the Government during each of the last 
three years; and 
(e) the other steps taken/being taken by the Government to curb the menace of monkeys in North 
Avenue, South Avenue and its adjacent Government offices? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND 
CLIMATE CHANGE  
(SHRI KIRTI VARDHAN SINGH) 
 
(a) to (e) The major monkey species involved in negative interactions in different parts of Delhi 
is the Rhesus macaque, which is not protected under the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 
1972. Accordingly, it is managed by local civic bodies using extant provisions of 
relevant laws/acts in force in their respective jurisdiction besides directions of the 
Honourable High Court of Delhi dated March 14, 2007. 
 
However, the Ministry provides financial assistance to State Governments and Union 
Territory Administrations under the Centrally Sponsored Scheme of Integrated 
Development of Wildlife Habitats for management of wildlife and its habitat in the 
country which inter-alia includes mitigation of human-wildlife conflict. The activities 
supported include procurement of early warning systems, construction and erection 
of physical barriers such as solar powered electric fencing, bio-fencing, trenches, 
boundary walls etc. to prevent depredation by wild animals which includes cattle 
lifting, crop damage, loss of life and property. Rapid Response Teams with 
community stewards are also deployed to mitigate Human-Wildlife Conflict. The 
details of funds released to States/UTs in the last three years are annexed herewith.

to them from the said Constituencies, districts and Madhya Pradesh; and 
 
(d) the details of the specific initiatives taken/being taken by the Government to increase 
participation of women in apprenticeship training and expand apprenticeship opportunities in 
manufacturing, engineering, logistics, agriculture-processing and service sectors, and established 
skill development and apprenticeship centres across the country and the said State and 
Constituencies?  
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) IN THE MINISTRY OF SKILL 
DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP 
 
(SHRI JAYANT CHAUDHARY) 
 

(a)  In order to strengthen collaboration with industries, MSMEs and technology companies for 
providing industry-aligned skill training across the country, including Bharatpur, Nabarangpur and 
Dewas- Shajapur Lok Sabha constituencies, the following specific steps have been taken by 
MSDE: 
 
 i.  National Council for Vocational Education and Training (NCVET) has been set up as an 
overarching regulator establishing regulations and standards to ensure quality in the 
Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) space. 
 ii.  The Awarding Bodies recognized by NCVET are expected to develop the qualifications as 
per industry demand and map them with the identified occupations as per the National 
Classification of Occupations, 2015 and obtain industry validations. 
 iii.  36 Sector Skill Councils (SSCs), led by industry leaders in the respective sectors, have 
been set up, which identify the skill development needs of respective sectors as well as to 
determine skill competency standards.  
iv.  Directorate General of Training (DGT) under the aegis of MSDE is implementing Flexi MoU 
Scheme and Dual System of Training (DST), which are meant to provide training to ITI 
students in industrial environment as per their requirements. 
 v.  Under PMKVY, the new age/future skills job -roles have been specially aligned with Industry 
4.0 requirements in areas like AI/ML, Robotics, Mechatronics, Drone Technology, etc. for 
upcoming market demand and industry requirements.  
vi.  DGT has introduced new age /future skills courses under CTS to provide training in 
emerging areas such as  5G Network Technician, Artificial Intelligence Programming 
Assistant, Cyber Security Assistant, Drone Technician etc.  
vii.  DGT has signed MoU with IT Tech companies like IBM, CISCO, Microsoft, AWS etc. to 
ensure industry linkages for the institutes at the state and regional levels. These 
partnerships facilitate the provision of technical and professional skills training in modern 
technologies.  
viii. The National Education Policy (NEP), 2020 envisages greater integration of vocational 
education with mainstream education an d promotes seamless mobility between academic 
and vocational pathways. In line with this vision, the Apprenticeship Embedded Degree 
Programme (AEDP), developed in collaboration with UGC and AICTE, enables students 
enrolled in degree and diploma programmes to undertake apprenticeship training as an 
integral part of their curriculum. The programme enhances employability, promotes 
outcome-based learning, strengthens industry -academia linkages and facilitates acquisition 
of industry-relevant skills.  
ix.  Kaushal Melas and Pradhan Mantri National Apprenticeship Melas (PMNAMs) are 
organised to facilitate placements and apprenticeship opportunities for the certified 
candidates.  
 
(b) The Government of India launched the National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme 
(NAPS) in August, 2016 with the objective of promoting apprenticeship training and increasing 
engagement of apprentices across the country. Since 2022 -23, the scheme continues as NAPS -
2. 
 
Apprenticeship training is conducted in actual work environments using the train ing facilities 
available with participating establishments including MSMEs, enabling hands -on-learning and 
industry exposure. 
 
To strengthen collaboration with industries, MSMEs and technology -driven companies, 
apprenticeship training is delivered through participating establishments under the provisions of 
the Apprentices Act, 1961. The scheme facilitates industry -led, on -the-job training through the 
National Apprenticeship Portal (www.apprenticeshipindia.gov.in), support from Regional 
Directorates of Skill Development & Entrepreneurship (RDSDEs), State Apprenticeship Advisers 
(SAAs) and empanelled Third Party Aggregators (TPAs). Further, Pradhan Mantri National 

Apprenticeship Melas (PMNAMs) are organized regularly to promote apprenticeship opportunities 
and strengthen industry participation, including MSMEs. 
 
The State/UT-wise details of apprentices engaged and participating establishments under NAPS -
2 are placed at Table-I of the Annexure , while the corresponding details for the Bharatpur, 
Nabarangpur, and Dewas–Shajapur Lok Sabha Constituencies from FY 2022-23 to FY 2026-
27 (up to June 2026) are placed at Table-II of the Annexure. 
 
Under NAPS-2, the Government provides partial stipend support to eligible apprentices engaged 
by establishments. The Government's share of stipend support is limited to 25% of the stipend 
paid, subject to a maximum of ₹1,500 per month per apprentice , which is disbursed directly 
into the bank account of the apprentice through the Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) mechanism. 
 
To expand apprenticeship opportunities, the Government has: 
• Simplified apprenticeship engagement through the National Apprenticeship Portal; 
• Promoted participation of industries and MSMEs; 
• Introduced digital processing of contracts, and stipend support; 
• Facilitated apprenticeship engagement through TPAs; 
• Conducted PMNAMs for mobilization of youth and industry participation; and 
• Expanded apprent iceship opportunities across  the Optional Trades  and Designated 
Trades. 
 
Sector-wise and district -wise apprentices engaged in Bharatpur, Nabarangpur and Dewas -
Shajapur Lok Sabha Constituencies under NAPS -2 from FY 2022 -23 to FY 2026 -27 (Upto June 
2026) are placed at Table-III of the Annexure. 
 
The number of unique establishments participating under NAPS -2 from FY 2022 -23 to FY 2026 -
27 (Upto June 2026) across all sectors, across the country, the concerned State, and in 
Bharatpur, Nabarangpur and Dewas -Shajapur Lok Sabha Constituencies are placed at Table-IV 
of the Annexure. 
 
(c) The details of apprentices benefited and stipend support disbursed under NAPS -2, 
including in Madhya Pradesh  and district-wise in the Bharatpur, Nabarangpur, and Dewas –
Shajapur Lok Sabha Constituencies, are placed at Table-V and Table-VI of the Annexure. 
 
(d) To increase participation of women in apprenticeship training and expand apprenticeship 
opportunities across sectors, the  National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme encourages 
engagement of apprentices, including women, across diverse sectors such as manufacturing, 
engineering, logistics, agriculture and allied activities, food processing, retail, healthcare, tourism 
and hospitality, IT-ITeS, electronics and other service sectors. 
 
The Government regularly organizes Pradhan Mantri National Apprenticeship Melas 
(PMNAMs) across the country, in one -third of the districts of each State every month, with a 
focus on mobilizing youth, including women candidates. Further, during stakeholder 
engagements with States, Regional Directorates of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship 
(RDSDEs), State Apprenticeship Advisers (SAAs), industries and Third -Party Aggregators 
(TPAs), special emphasis is placed on increasing the participation of women apprentices across 
sectors. 
 
To enhance availability of apprenticeship opportunities, the Apprentices Act, 1961  was 
amended in 2014 to introduce Optional Trades , enabling industries to design apprenticeship 
programmes aligned to their specific skill requirements. 
 
The scheme also promotes safe, inclusive and conducive training environments for all 
apprentices including women apprentices. Under Section 14 of the Apprentices Act, 1961 , 

apprentices are covered by the relevant safety, health and welfare provisions applicable to 
workers under the Factories Act, 1948  and the Mines Act, 1952 , as applicable. Consequently, 
apprentices are entitled to workplace safety measures, welfare facilities and protective provisions 
similar to regular employees. In addition, apprentices are covered under the Sexual Harassment 
of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013 (POSH Act) . 
Further, Section 15 of the Apprentices Act, 1961 regulates working hours and leave provisions. 
Apprentices aged 18 years and above are trained during normal working hours of the 
establishment, while working hours for apprentices below 18 years are ordinarily restricted 
between 8:00 AM and 6:00 PM , except where specifically permitted by the concerned 
Apprenticeship Adviser.

MINISTRY OF CORPORATE AFFAIRS

UPGRADATION OF THE INSOLVENCY ECOSYSTEM 
QUESTION 
2327. Shri Praveen Khandelwal: 
 
Will the Minister of CORPORATE AFFAIRS                      
be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government has reviewed the functioning of the pre -packaged 
insolvency resolution process for micro, small and medium enterprises under the 
Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code and the measures taken to improve its uptake;  
 
(b) if so, the details thereof, including the status of the proposed integrated technology 
platform for the insolvency ecosystem and e -filing before the National Company Law 
Tribunal; 
 
(c) the details of corporate insolvency cases admitted, resolved and the average 
resolution time recorded during the last three years, year-wise; 
 
(d) whether the Government has taken or proposes to take any special measures for 
faster, low cost insolvency resolution and creditor protection for small trading 
enterprises, including those in commercial hubs such as Chandni Chowk in Delhi; and  
 
(e) if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor? 
 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CORPORATE AFFAIRS AND MINISTER OF 
STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS  
 
[SHRI HARSH MALHOTRA] 
 
 
(a) and (b): Yes Sir.  The functioning of the Pre-Packaged Insolvency Resolution Process 
(PPIRP) for Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) was reviewed based on the 
experience gained in its implementation and stakeholder feedback. Based on the 
review, amendments were introduced vide the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code 
(Amendment) Act, 2026 to strengthen the PPIRP framework including , inter alia, the 
following: 
 
(i)The existing provisions relating to information to be furnished along with the 
application to initiate Pre-packaged Insolvency Resolution Process (PPIRP) have been 
simplified to give greater flexibility and ease of the documentation process for MSMEs 
to use the PPIRP route to insolvency.  

 
(ii) the threshold for initiation of PPIRP has been relaxed from 66% to 51% of voting 
share of unrelated financial creditors, thereby lowering barriers for MSMEs to access 
the mechanism. 
 
The System Integrator for the Integrated Platform for IBC Ecosystem (iPIE) has been 
onboarded.  The e-filing before the National Company Law Tribunal is done through the 
existing e-court system. 
  
(c): The year-wise details of corporate insolvency cases admitted , resolved and the 
average resolution time recorded during the last three years is at Annexure. 
 
Time taken to resolve each case depends on circumstances and complexity of each 
case, nature of evidence, number of Interlocutory Applications (IAs), stay by the higher 
courts, cooperation of stake holders and adjournments etc. 
 
 
(d) and (e): No such proposal is under consideration.
