MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2328 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 03.08.2026 
 
Green Credit Programme 
 
2328.  SHRI BHARTRUHARI MAHTAB: 
 SHRI DINESHBHAI MAKWANA: 
 SHRI BALABHADRA MAJHI: 
 SHRI DILIP SAIKIA: 
 SHRI HARIBHAI PATEL: 
 SHRI BIDYUT BARAN MAHATO: 
 SHRI TEJASVI SURYA: 
 SHRI LUMBARAM CHOUDHARY: 
 SHRI P C MOHAN: 
 SHRI DAMODAR AGRAWAL: 
 SMT. KAMLESH JANGDE: 
 SHRI KHAGEN MURMU: 
 SHRI SATISH KUMAR GAUTAM: 
 SHRI RAVINDRA SHUKLA ALIAS RAVI KISHAN: 
 SHRI MANOJ TIWARI: 
 SHRI JANARDAN MISHRA: 
 SHRI BHARATSINHJI SHANKARJI DABHI: 
 SHRI BIBHU PRASAD TARAI: 
 DR. SANJAY JAISWAL: 
 
Will the Minister of ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE be pleased to 
state: 
 
(a) whether the Government has assessed the ecological outcomes and environmental 
benefits achieved since the operationalisation of the Green Credit Programme and, if so, 
the key findings thereof, including the progress made in Nabarangpur Lok Sabha 
Constituency; 
(b) whether the Government has developed a framework for monitoring, verification and 
long-term ecological assessment of activities carried out under the Green Credit 
Programme and, if so, the details thereof, including its implementation in the said 
Constituency; 
(c) whether the Government proposes to expand the Green Credit Programme beyond tree 
plantation and water conservation to other environmental sectors, if so, the details 
thereof; and 
(d) whether the said Constituency is proposed to be covered under such initiatives and if so, 
the details thereof, including the proposed activities and expected benefits for it? 
 
 
  

ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND 
CLIMATE CHANGE  
(SHRI KIRTI VARDHAN SINGH) 
 
(a) to 
(d) 
The Green Credit Programme is an innovative mechanism to incentivise 
environmentally positive actions and to promote the objectives of Mission LiFE 
(Lifestyle for Environment) movement, which aims at encouraging sustainable 
lifestyles by driving community towards behavioural changes that support 
environment-friendly actions. The Green Credit Programme aims to increase 
green cover, enhance carbon sequestration, restore degraded lands and reduce 
carbon footprint through the adoption of environment-friendly technologies and 
practices. 
 
The Central Government has notified Green Credit Rules, 2023 on 12th October 
2023 under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 to encourage voluntary 
environmental positive actions resulting in issuance of Green Credits. Under the 
Green Credit Programme, the modality for tree plantation and eco-restoration of 
degraded forest lands has been notified on 22nd February 2024 and subsequently 
revised on 29th August 2025. A Green Credit Programme Portal (https://moefcc-
gcp.in/) has been developed for the purpose. 
 
The Indian Council of Forestry Research and Education, Dehradun is the 
Administrator under the Green Credit Programme and is responsible for the 
effective implementation of the Programme, including its management, operation 
and issuance of green credits. 
 
The Green Credit Programme aims to restore degraded forest lands through the 
active participation of public and private sector entities. The degraded forest land 
parcels proposed to be taken up under the Green Credit Programme are selected 
and registered by the State Forest Department after due verification on the ground.  
 
The Green Credits can be claimed by an applicant only after minimum five years 
of restoration work have been completed and a minimum canopy density of forty 
per cent has been achieved. A five-year establishment period is prescribed to allow 
the planted seedlings and natural regenerations to mature and develop adequate 
canopy cover, so as to achieve the prescribed 40 per cent canopy density, 
corresponding to a moderately dense forest.  
 
The forest restoration activities undertaken under the programme aim to enhance 
biodiversity and improve the productivity of forest resources. The restoration of 
degraded forest lands aims to benefit local communities by increasing the 
availability of timber, non-timber forest produce, fodder, water, and other 
ecosystem services. 
 
The "designated agency" designated under the Green Credit Programme shall 
conduct verification of the claim for the Green Credits and submit report to the 
Administrator as regard to the verification of the activities undertaken by an 
applicant for issuance of green credit. 

 
A comprehensive Manual on Monitoring and Reporting of Restoration Activities 
under the Green Credit Programme to facilitate effective implementation and 
monitoring of the programme. 
 
As on date, there is no land parcel registered on the GCP Portal under Green Credit 
Programme by the Odisha Forest Department in Nabarangpur Lok Sabha 
Constituency

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2329 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 03.08.2026 
FEATURES AND OBJECTIVES OF PM-VBRY 
 
2329. SHRI JASHUBHAI BHILUBHAI RATHVA: 
 
Will the Minister of LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT be pleased to 
state:  
 
(a)the details of key features and objectives of the Pradhan Mantri 
Viksit Bharat Rozgar  Yojana (PM -VBRY) including sectoral focus 
and target job creation; 
(b)the details of registration and  onboarding mechanism for 
establishments and workers  including employer incentives and 
digital portal integration; 
(c)whether the Government has planned any monitoring or 
assessment framework to  evaluate the outcomes of the scheme 
including its impact on e mployment levels and formal  sector 
absorption; and 
(d)if so, the details thereof? 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT 
(SUSHRI SHOBHA KARANDLAJE) 
 
(a) to (d): The Union Cabinet, on 1 July 2025, approved the 
Employment Linked Incentive (ELI) Scheme, titled the Pradhan Mantri 
Viksit Bharat Rojgar Yojana (PMVBRY), to promote employment 
generation, enhance employability, and strengthen social security 
across all sec tors, with a particular focus on the manufacturing 
sector. 
 
  The scheme has a registration period of two years from 
01.08.2025 to 31.07.2027 and has a budgetary outlay of ₹99,446 
Crore. 
  The scheme comprises of two parts i.e. Part A and Part B 
and focuses on providing support to both employees and employers 
by way of incentives. 
Contd..2/- 
 
 

:: 2 :: 
  Under Part A of the scheme, the first -time employees of 
both existing and new establishments shall be eligible for an 
incentive equivalent to one month’s EP F wage, subject to a 
maximum of ₹15,000. This incentive will be payable in two 
instalments during the first year of employment. The first instalment, 
up to ₹7,500, shall be disbursed after completion of six months of 
continuous employment. Eligibility for the second instalment shall 
arise after completion of twelve months of employment and 
successful completion of the prescribed Financial Literacy 
Programme. This second instalment shall be credited to an 
appropriate savings instrument/savings account for a specified 
period.  
  The scheme aims to incentivise creation of more than 3.5 
Crore jobs all across the country, over a period of 2 years. The 
scheme provides for incentives for 1.92 crore eligible First time 
employees under Part A. Incentive for creation of approximately 2.59 
crore additional jobs to employers is provided for under Part B of the 
scheme.  
  The Employees' Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) is the 
implementing agency for the scheme. A dedicated portal 
(pmvbry.epfindia.gov.in) has been developed to facilitate all scheme-
related processes. 
  As on 29.07.2026, a total of 5,52,327 establishments have 
been registered across the country under the Pradhan Mantri Viksit 
Bharat Rojgar Yojana (PMVBRY). 
  For effective implementation of the scheme, a ro bust 
monitoring framework has been instituted. A Steering Committee 
with representation from various labour intensive and related 
Ministries/Department and an internal Executive Committee have 
been constituted to ensure effective monitoring of the scheme. 
  The Scheme also provides for a mid -term evaluation for 
necessary course correction and an end -term evaluation to assess 
the Scheme outcome by a third party.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
DEPARTMENT OF SCHOOL EDUCATION & LITERACY 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2330 
ANSWERED ON 03.08.2026 
 
Establishment of Navodaya Vidyalayas for Providing Technical Education 
 
†2330. Shri Arun Kumar Sagar:  
 
Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state:  
 
(a) whether the Government proposes to establish Navodaya Vidyalayas to provide 
technical education to poor students in every district of the backward areas of the 
country particularly in Shahjahanpur of Uttar Pradesh;  
 
(b) if so, the details thereof; and  
 
(c) if not, the reasons therefor? 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(SHRI JAYANT CHAUDHARY) 
 
(a) to (c): The Navodaya Vidyalaya Scheme envisages for opening of one Navodaya 
Vidyalaya (NV) in each district of the country. Opening of new NVs in uncovered 
districts is a continuous process which depends on the willingness of the concerned 
State Government/UT admi nistration to make available requisite suitable land, free 
of cost, for construction of the permanent building and making available required 
temporary building, free of rent, to run the Vidyalaya till the permanent building is 
constructed. Sanction and ope ning of new NVs depends on approval by the 
competent authority as per extant procedures. As on date, all 75 districts of Uttar 
Pradesh have been covered under the scheme and 76 NVs are functional in these 
districts. 
As per information received from Navodaya Vidyalaya Sam iti (NVS), NVs 
students are taught basic Computer Science (ICT) from Classes VI to XII, through 
smart classrooms, in accordance with the curriculum and guidelines prescribed by 
the CBSE. Skill -based subjects are also offered in all NV s as per the CBSE 
curriculum and the choices exercised by the students. Artificial Intelligence (AI) and 
Coding & Computational Thinking (CT) have also been introduced from the 
academic session 2026–27 in accordance with the CBSE guidelines. Skill Labs have 
also been established in NVs under various projects, such as in collaboration with 
CBSE under Skilling at Schools project with World Bank, NVS CBSE project, under 
CSR support of Tata Motors Limited and through Ministry of Skill Development & 

Entrepreneurship (MSDE) . Total 800 Skill Labs in 400 NVs, including in 
Shahjahanpur district, Uttar Pradesh, were established through project of MSDE.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF CULTURE 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2331 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 03.08.2026 
 
 
CONSERVATION AND MAINTENANCE OF PROTECTED MONUMENTS 
 
 
 
Will the Minister of CULTURE be pleased to state: 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
2331. SHRI RAMASAHAYAM RAGHURAM REDDY: 
SHRI CAPTAIN VIRIATO FERNANDES: 
SHRI RAJESH NARANBHAI CHUDASAMA: 
SMT. JYOTSNA CHARANDAS MAHANT : 
(a) the details of number of centrally protected monuments under the  Archaeological 
Survey of India (ASI) that have been identified as requiring urgent conservation, 
repair or protection from encroachment, State/UT-wise, particularly district-wise in 
Chhattisgarh such as the Laxman Temple in Sirpur and Bhoramdeo Temple; 
(b) the details of budget allocation and actual expenditure for the maintenance and 
repair of ASI monuments, State/UT-wise, particularly in Chhattisgarh since 2022; 
(c) the details of current sanctioned strength and vacancies  in   ASI,  category-wise,  
including archaeologists, conservation assistants, engineers, site-security staff and 
other technical staff including Raipur Circle; 
(d) whether the Government has assessed the impact of manpower and financial 
constraints on the conservation and maintenance of protected monuments, and if so, 
the details thereof; 
(e) the details of monuments currently entrusted to private entities, corporate bodies or 
other organisations for maintenance, conservation or visitor management, State/UT-
wise; 
(f) whether any historical monuments in Chhattisgarh have been proposed or entrusted 
to private entities under the 'Adopt a Heritage' scheme for visitor management and 
upkeep; 
(g) whether  the  Government  has  identified any instances  of   non-compliance,  
inadequate maintenance or violation of prescribed conservation norms by such 
entities especially in the form of construction of structures in protected areas under 
ASI, particularly in village Old Goa/Velha Goa in Goa; and 
 
(h) if so, the details thereof and action taken thereon? 

 
ANSWER 
      MINISTER OF CULTURE AND  TOURISM  
(SHRI GAJENDRA SINGH SHEKHAWAT) 
 
(a) There are 3688 centrally protected monuments and sites across the country including 
the Laxman Temple in Sirpur and Bhoramdeo Temple in Chhattisgarh  under the 
jurisdiction of the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI). ASI undertakes conservation 
of these Monuments and sites as per the National Policy for Conservation, 2014 and 
the Ancient Monuments and Archaeological Sites and Remains (AMASR) Act, 1958, 
along with the rules framed thereunder. Conservation and day to day maintenance, up 
keeping of all these monuments and sites are carried out regularly as per the need 
and availability of resources. All these monuments and sites are in a good state of 
preservation. 
(b) 
  
 
  
 
The details of budget allocated and expenditure incurred for the conservation, 
preservation and maintenance of centrally protected monuments in the country, 
State/UT-wise, including Chhattisgarh from 2021-22 to 2025-26 are given at 
Annexure-I. 
(c) The details of archaeologists, conservation assistants, engineers and other technical 
staff in the Archaeological Survey of India and at Raipur Circle are at Annexure-II and 
Annexure-III respectively. 
(d) The adequacy of manpower in the Archaeological Survey of India is reviewed on a 
continuous basis through the sanctioned strength of various Circles, which is 
determined keeping in view the functional requirements, number of Centrally 
Protected Monuments (CPMs)/sites under their jurisdiction and other administrative 
considerations. Deployment of available manpower is also reviewed from time to time 
to ensure conservation, maintenance and management of centrally protected 
monuments and sites. 
(e) Archaeological Survey of India (ASI), under the provisions of the Ancient Monuments 
and Archaeological Sites and Remains Act, 1958, is mandated to protect, conserve, 
preserve and maintain Centrally Protected Monuments and Sites. Under the Adopt A 
Heritage 2.0 programme, ASI facilitates the development, provision and maintenance 
of identified visitor amenities at protected monuments through engagement with public 
and private entities. However, the responsibilities of such entities are strictly confined 
to non-conservation activities, whereas conservation and preservation of Centrally 
Protected Monuments/Sites are carried out exclusively by ASI. As on date, 31 MoUs 
have been signed under the programme. The details are at Annexure-IV. 
(f) As far as the Adopt A Heritage 2.0programme is concerned, no proposal regarding 
any protected monument in Chhattisgarh has been received by ASI from any entity. 
(g) 
 & 
(h) 
No private agency has been entrusted the work of conservation and preservation of 
Centrally Protected Monuments in Old Goa by ASI.

MINISTRY OF LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT

UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2332 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 03.08.2026 
RESTORATION AND UPGRADATION OF ESI MEDICAL 
INSTITUTIONS IN ERNAKULAM. 
 
2332. SHRI HIBI EDEN: 
 
Will the Minister of LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT be pleased to 
state:  
 
(a)whether the Government is aware of the deteriorated condition of 
the Employees' State Insurance (ESI) Hospital at Ernakulam North 
and if so, the details thereof; 
(b)whether the proposal f or construction of a new 100 -bedded ESI 
Hospital at Ernakulam North has been approved or is under 
consideration and if so, the present status of the proposal, the 
estimated cost, the timeline for commencement and completion of 
the project along with the steps being taken by the Government to 
expedite the same; 
(c)whether the Government is aware that the ESI Dispensary and sub-
store at Fort Kochi suffered extensive damage in a recent fire 
incident and if so, the details thereof; and 
(d)whether the Government proposes to provide a suitable temporary 
alternative building for the functioning of the ESI Dispensary at Fort 
Kochi until the damaged buildings are restored and if so, the details 
thereof and if not, the reasons therefor? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT 
(SUSHRI SHOBHA KARANDLAJE) 
 
(a) to (d): The Employees' State Insurance Corporation (ESIC) 
has approved the construction of a new 100 -bed hospital at 
Ernakulam North as the existing hospital building has become 
outdated, congested, and  inadequate to support future 
healthcare demands. 
  The concept plan has already been cleared, and the 
construction work has been assigned to the Central Public 
Works Department (CPWD). According to the preliminary 
estimate provided by CPWD, the project wi ll cost 
approximately ₹232.00 crore and is expected to be completed 
within three years. 
Contd..2/- 

 
:: 2 :: 
 
  The ESI Dispensary building at Fort Kochi, 
constructed in 1966, suffered significant damage in a major 
fire incident. The fire completely destroy ed the section 
housing the RDD Sub Store, two rooms of the dispensary, and 
the associated electrical installations. 
 
   Meanwhile, the ESI Dispensary has been temporarily 
shifted to the ESI Dispensary at Thoppumpady, located about 
5 km away, to ensure unin terrupted healthcare services, till 
restoration of original building of Fort Kochi dispensary.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2333 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 03.08.2026 
 
Forest Conservation Schemes 
 
2333. SHRI VIJAYAKUMAR ALIAS VIJAY VASANTH: 
 
Will the Minister of ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE be pleased to 
state: 
 
(a) whether forest-dependent communities are involved in conservation efforts, if so, the 
details thereof and if not, the reasons for lack of community participation; 
(b) whether funds allocated under forest conservation schemes have been fully utilised, if so, 
the details thereof and if not, the reasons for underutilisation; 
(c) whether climate change has exacerbated forest degradation and forest fires, if so, the 
details thereof and measures taken to mitigate such risks; 
(d) whether the Government has assessed the impact of mining activities in forest areas, if 
so. the details thereof and the steps taken to regulate environmentally sensitive zones; 
(e) whether wildlife habitats are being adversely affected due to shrinking forest cover, if so, 
the details thereof and conservation strategies implemented to protect biodiversity, and 
(f) whether policies exist to prevent fragmentation of forests due to infrastructure expansion, 
if so, the details thereof and effectiveness of such measures? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND 
CLIMATE CHANGE  
(SHRI KIRTI VARDHAN SINGH) 
 
(a) Forest-dependent communities are actively involved in forest conservation and 
sustainable forest management through various programmes and institutional 
mechanisms. Emphasis is given on promoting participatory forest management is 
by involving local communities through Joint Forest Management Committees 
(JFMCs) and Eco-Development Committees (EDCs) around Protected Areas 
constituted by State Governments. These institutions participate in various 
activities for protection of forests including preventing illegal felling, management 
of forest fires, afforestation activities, restoration of degraded forests, and 
sustainable management of forest resources.  
 
Further, the Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition 
of Forest Rights) Act, 2006 recognize and vest forest rights in eligible forest-
dwelling communities and empower Gram Sabhas to protect, regenerate, 
conserve, and manage community forest resources for sustainable use, thereby 
strengthening the role of local communities in forest conservation. 
 
 

(b) & 
(c) 
In order to increase the forest and tree cover and restore degraded forest lands the 
Ministry provides technical and financial support to the States and Union 
Territories (UTs) under various schemes and programmes such as National 
Mission for a Green India (GIM), Compensatory Afforestation Fund Management 
and Planning Authority (CAMPA), Nagar Van Yojana, Mangrove Initiative for 
Shoreline Habitats & Tangible Incomes (MISHTI), etc. 
 
In addition, the National Action Plan on Forest Fires, 2018 provides a 
comprehensive framework for prevention, detection, control and management of 
forest fires through capacity building, use of modern technology, community 
participation and strengthening of forest fire management systems. The Ministry 
provides financial assistance to the States and Union Territories under the 
Centrally Sponsored Scheme, ‘Forest Fire Prevention and Management’ for 
integrated management of forest fire. 
 
(d) The Government assesses the environmental and ecological impacts of mining 
proposals in forest areas through the statutory appraisal processes prescribed under 
the Van (Sanrakshan Evam Samvardhan) Adhiniyam, 1980, the Environment 
(Protection) Act, 1986, the Wild Life (Protection) Act, 1972, and other applicable 
laws and rules. Mining proposals in forest areas are examined on a case-to-case 
basis, taking into account site-specific ecological features, likely impacts on 
wildlife and habitats, and the mitigation measures proposed. 
 
 
(e) 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
(f) 
As per India State of Forest Report, (ISFR) 2023, the forest and tree cover of the 
country is 8,27,356.95 square kilometer which is 25.17% of the total geographical 
area of the country. The forest and tree cover of the country has increased by 
1445.81 square kilometer as compared to the last assessment of ISFR 2021.   
 
A network of protected areas namely, National Parks, Sanctuaries, Conservation 
Reserves and Community Reserves covering important wildlife habitats have been 
notified all over the country under the provisions of the Wild Life (Protection) 
Act, 1972, to conserve wild animals and their habitats. The number of Protected 
Areas have increased to 1134. Further, there are 58 Tiger Reserves and 33 
Elephant Reserves. In addition, for maintaining the ecological connectivity, 32 
tiger corridors and 150 Elephant corridors have been identified.  
 
The diversion of forest land for non-forestry purposes, including infrastructure 
projects, is regulated under the provisions of the Van (Sanrakshan Evam 
Samvardhan) Adhiniyam, 1980 and the rules and guidelines issued thereunder. 
Proposals involving diversion of forest land are examined on a case-to-case basis 
taking into consideration forestry, wildlife and environmental perspectives. While 
considering such proposals, emphasis is given to minimise the requirement of 
forest land and to avoid or reduce fragmentation of forests.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2334 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 03.08.2026 
Green India Mission 
2334. SHRI ATUL GARG: 
Will the Minister of ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE be pleased to 
state: 
(a)  whether the Government has evaluated the afforestation targets achieved under the 
National Mission for a Green India (GIM) during the last three years in Uttar Pradesh; 
(b)  if so, the details thereof, including the total forest and non-forest areas brought under green 
cover and the specific landscapes targeted in the State; 
(c)  the details of total Central funds allocated, released, utilised and the balance available with 
the State implementing agency in Uttar Pradesh during the last one year; 
(d)  whether the Government has noted low survival rates of plantations due to adverse climatic 
conditions or inadequate post-plantation care in certain districts; and 
(e)  the steps being taken by the Government to strengthen the role of Joint Forest Management 
Committees in executing and monitoring these greening projects in Uttar Pradesh? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND 
CLIMATE CHANGE  
(SHRI KIRTI VARDHAN SINGH) 
(a) to (c) The National Mission for a Green India (GIM), one of the nine Missions under the 
National Action Plan on Climate Change (NAPCC), aims to protect, restore and 
enhance forest and tree cover while contributing to climate change mitigation and 
adaptation through plantation and ecosystem restoration in identified landscapes. 
Under GIM, activities are implemented based on approved Perspective Plans and 
Annual Plans of Operation submitted by the States and approved by the National 
Executive Council. 
The implementation of GIM is monitored through periodic review meetings and 
progress reports submitted by the States. In the State of Uttar Pradesh, 
implementation of GIM activities commenced in 2023-24, and an area of 4,202.25 
hectares has been taken up so far under eco-restoration in approved degraded forest 
landscapes. The activities are primarily undertaken in degraded landscapes based on 
the approved perspective plan of the state. During the last financial year 2025-26, a 
total amount of Rs. 3.30 crore was allocated/released to the State of Uttar Pradesh 
under the National Mission for a Green India (GIM) and same has been fully utilized 
by the State.  
(d)  Monitoring of plantations follows a multi-tiered approach involving both Central 
and State mechanisms. State Forest Departments undertake annual physical 
verification, geo-tagged monitoring and third-party inspections. Corrective 
measures, including gap filling and maintenance, are undertaken based on survival 
assessments. 

(e) The implementation of GIM is undertaken with the active participation of local 
communities through institutions such as Joint Forest Management Committees 
(JFMCs). These committees play an important role in planning and implementation, 
of afforestation and eco-restoration activities. The Ministry also supports capacity 
building, participatory micro-planning and community engagement to strengthen the 
role of JFMCs in sustainable forest management.

measures to promote the inclusion of women,  rural, tribal and para -

greater participation of  the private sector through Public -Private 
Partnerships (PPPs), Corporate Social Responsibility  (CSR), sports 
entrepreneurship and startups for strengthening the sports ecosystem 
in the Country, State/UT-wise, particularly Akola and Tribal district of 
Palghar in Maharashtra and if so, the details thereof; 
(e) whether the Government proposes to develop modern sports 
facilities, training centres and  sports infrastructure to nurture sports 
talent in areas such as Darbhanga and if so, the details thereof; and

policy, particularly with regard to India's preparations for the 2032 and 
2036 Olympic Games and making India into a  global sport ing 
powerhouse and whether the Government proposes to establish 
additional sports infrastructure and Khelo India Centre in Jalgaon Lok 
Sabha Constituency to support the said  Games and if so, the details 
thereof?

 THE MINISTER OF YOUTH AFFAIRS AND SPORTS 
[DR MANSUKH MANDAVIYA] 
(a):  Yes. The Khelo Bharat Niti 2025 aims at building a strong, 
inclusive, and performance-driven sports ecosystem in India. The Union 
Government, implements the Khelo Bharat Niti 2025, through its 
ongoing schemes and programmes, which operate within defined 
guidelines and reporting frameworks. 
Under the the Khelo India Scheme, Shimla Lok Sabha Constituency has 
03 operational KICs. Similarly, in Palghar district in Maharashtra, 01 
Khelo India Centre is fully functional. The details are available in public 
domain on the dashboard of Khelo India 
(https://dashboard.kheloindia.gov.in/). Further, a total of 349 
infrastructure projects have been sanctioned, the details of which are 
available at https://mdsd.kheloindia.gov.in/. 
(b):  Khelo Bharat Niti, 2025 provides a whole -of-Government 
framework for sports development through convergence among Central 
Ministries, National Sports Federations (NSFs), educational institutions, 
the private sector and other stakeholders. Grassroot training is 
delivered through 1,066 operational KICs nationwide. In Darbhanga 
(Bihar), 01 KIC for Football trains 30 athletes; in Akola  (Maharashtra), 
01 KIC for Boxing trains 30 athletes; and in Jalgaon (Maharashtra),  01 
KIC for Archery is operational with 37 Athletes. There are also 3 Khelo

India Accredited Academies in Jalgaon district, in Badminton, Shooting 
and Swimming discipline.

receives an annual support package of ₹6.28 lakh covering c oaching, 
sports science, equipment, boarding, insurance and a monthly Out -of-
Pocket Allowance of ₹10,000. 
(c):  Under the current Los Angeles 2028 (LA 2028) Paralympic Cycle, 
a total of 62 para -athletes has been inducted under the TOPS, 
comprising 41 men a nd 21 women as compared to Paris 2024 
Paralympic Cycle, where 59 para-athletes were supported under TOPS, 
including 40 men and 19 women. 
Athletes inducted under TOPS for Para Sports (Core Group) receive a 
monthly Out -of-Pocket Allowance (OPA) of ₹50,000, a long with 
individualized support based on their training and competition 
requirements. This support includes financial assistance towards 
foreign training and competition exposure, sportsspecific equipment 
and kits, remuneration for coaches and sports science experts (such as 
physiotherapists, strength and conditioning trainers, and nutritionists), 
medical support, and assistive devices such as prostheses, 
wheelchairs, and other specialized equipment, wherever required. 
(d): The Government encourages greate r participation of the private 
sector in strengthening the sports ecosystem through initiatives such 
as Khelo India  Accredited Academies and Corporate Social 
Responsibility (CSR). As per the  Office Memorandum dated 18.06.2026 
issued by the Department of Pu blic Enterprises, Government of India, 
'Development of Sporting Activities' has been identified as a common 
CSR theme for Central Public Sector Enterprises (CPSEs). The identified 
areas include development of sports infrastructure, provision of sports 
equipment, access to professional coaching, promotion of sports and 
nurturing of sportspersons. 

Page 5 of 5 
 
Further, under the Khelo India Scheme, 364 Khelo India Accredited 
Academies have been accredited across the country, including 46 in 
Maharashtra, thereby promoting private sector participation in athlete 
training and development. 
(e):  New training centres are established subject to receipt of 
proposals from the respective State Governments/other stakeholders 
and fulfilment of the standard/feasibility criteria relati ng to availability 
of infrastructure, sporting ecosystem, talent pool and other operational 
criteria. 
Financial assistance for creation and upgradation of sports 
infrastructure is provided under the Khelo India Scheme and NSDF. 
Details are available in public domain on the dashboards of the Ministry 
at https://mdsd.kheloindia.gov.in. Currently, one Khelo India Centre in 
Football discipline is operational in Darbhanga with 30 trainees. 
(f):  Khelo Bharat Niti aims to transform India into a global sporting 
powerhouse by strengthening grassroots talent identification, sports 
infrastructure, athlete support and governance, with a view to 
improving India's performance at the Olympic, Paralympic, Asian and 
Commonwealth Games and supporting preparations for the 203 6 
Olympic Games. Presently, one Khelo India Centre is operational in 
Jalgaon catering to 37 athletes. Further, under the Khelo India Scheme, 
currently there is a Khelo India Centre in Jalgaon in the boxing 
discipline which caters to 37 athletes.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF CULTURE 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION No. 2337 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 03.08.2026 
 
NMCMR IN WAYANAD 
 
2337. Smt. Priyanka Gandhi Vadra: 
 
          Will the Minister of CULTUREbe pleased to state:- 
 
(a) whether the Government is taking initiative to document, preserve and 
safeguard both, tangible and intangible cultural heritage and if so, the details 
thereof; 
 
(b) the details of cultural assets mapped in Wayanad Lok Sabha Constituency, 
village-wise including demographic profiles, artists and art practices under the 
National Mission on Cultural Mapping and Roadmap (NMCMR); 
 
(c) the details of initiatives taken to support artisans and improve livelihoods, 
including through skill upgradation and marketing, especially in the said 
Constituency; 
 
(d) whether the Government proposes to promote handicraft based rural tourism 
initiatives and if so, the details thereof; and 
 
(e) the details of craft villages in India and pending proposals for recognition, if 
any? 
 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF CULTURE AND TOURISM 
(SHRI GAJENDRA SINGH SHEKHAWAT) 
 
(a) The National Mission on Cultural Mapping (NMCM) aims to preserve and 
safeguard India's diverse tangible and intangible cultural heritage through 
systematic documentation and cultural mapping. 
 
The Mera Gaon Meri Dharohar (MGMD) initiative under NMCM culturally 
maps tangible and intangible cultural heritage at the village level across 
States/UTs. It comprehensively documents a wide range of cultural elements 
prevalent across villages coveringheritage sites, art forms, prominent artists, 
oral traditions, beliefs and customs, historical significance, local landmarks, 
fairs and festivals, traditional dress, ornaments and traditional food, wherever 
available.  
 
At present, cultural profiles of approximately 6.34 lakh villages have been 
documented under the MGMD initiative. 
 

(b) The cultural profiles of villages falling within the Wayanad Lok Sabha 
Constituency have been documented under various categories on the MGMD 
Portal. These entail cultural significance, heritage places, fairs and festivals, 
traditional art and craft, tradition food, dress and ornaments, beliefs and 
customs, prominent artists, geographic and demographic profile, as well as 
developmental profile.  
 
This information is recorded on the MGMD web-portal under village-profiles 
and not as per individual elements. Accordingly, separate category-wise 
consolidated data are not maintained. However, a representative list of artists 
and art forms mapped in districts of the said constituency has been given at 
Annexure – I. 
 
 
(c) The objective of MGMD is the documentation of cultural heritage at the village 
level. Currently, there is no provision under the Mission for integration of this 
database with economic or skill development initiatives. 
 
 
(d) The MGMD web-portal functions as a digital repository of village-level cultural 
data. However, no specific initiative for promoting handicraft-based rural 
tourism has been undertaken under the Mission so far. 
 
(e) The mandate of MGMD is to document cultural assets, including craft activities 
practised in villages, wherever available, and not to categorise or recognise craft 
villages.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
DEPARTMENT OF HIGHER EDUCATION 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION No. 2338 
ANSWERED ON 03.08.2026 
 
Limited Access to Higher Education among Tribal Students 
 
2338. Dr. Kirsan Namdeo: 
 
Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government has conducted any assessment regarding the low Gross Enrolment Ratio 
(GER), high dropout rates and limited access to higher education among tribal students in the 
Gadchiroli-Chimur Lok Sabha Constituency, particularly in remote and Left Wing Extremism-affected 
areas, if so, the details thereof; 
 
(b) the details of Central Government -funded educational institutions, including Eklavya Model 
Residential Schools (EMRSs), Kendriya Vidyalayas, Navodaya Vidyalayas, deg ree colleges, hostels, 
digital learning centres and skill-based higher education facilities established or sanctioned in the said 
Constituency during the last five years, year-wise; 
 
(c) whether the Government proposes to establish additional higher educat ional institutions, tribal 
hostels, coaching centres for competitive examinations, digital libraries and career guidance centres to 
improve access to quality education for tribal and rural students in the Constituency; and 
 
(d) if so, the details thereof along with the timeline fixed for its implementation and if not, the reasons 
therefor? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(DR. SUKANTA MAJUMDAR) 
 
(a): Education being in the Concurrent List, enhancing educational facilities  is the responsibility of 
both the Central and State Governments. 
 
As per All India Survey on Higher Education (AISHE)  2023-24, the n umber of Higher 
Education Institutions (HEIs) are 7,893 and the enrolment of Schedule Tribe students is 2.25 lakh in 
the State of  Maharashtra, out of which 426 HEIs  and 19.6 thousand enrolments  are in 3 districts of 
Maharashtra (Chandrapur, Gadchiroli and Gondia districts). The Gross Enrolment Ratio (GER) in the 
state of Maharashtra for Schedule Tribe students has increased to 19.1 in 2023-24 from 15.7 in 2019-
20. 
 
(b) As per AISHE 2023-24, there are 9 Centrally Funded HEIs in the State of Maharashtra  and there 
are 311 colleges and 114 hostels in the 3 districts of Maharashtra (Chandrapur, Gadchiroli and Gondia). 

In the state of Maharashtra, there are 39 sanctioned Eklavya Model Residential Schools (EMRSs) out 
of which 9 EMRSs are sanctioned /functional in 3 districts of Maharashtra (Chandrapur, Gadchiroli 
and Gondia). 
 
As per Unified District Information System for Education Plus (UDISE+) 2025 -26, there are 2  
Kendriya Vidyalayas (KVs) and 3 Jawahar Navodaya Vidyalayas (JNVs) in 3 districts of Maharashtra 
(Chandrapur, Gadchiroli and Gondia). 
 
The major initiatives of Central Government to ensure equitable digital access of education in all States 
are as under: 
 
Under Samagra Shiksha, financial assistance is provided to States/UTs, including rural, tribal and 
economically backward areas, inter -alia for setting up of ICT labs and Smart Classrooms in 
Government and Government Aided Schools having classes VI to XII. 
 
(c) & (d) The government has launched the third phase of RUSA in June 2023 in the form of Pradhan 
Mantri Uchchatar Shiksha Abhiyan (PM-USHA), with an outlay of Rs.12926.10 crore for the period 
2023-24 to 2025-26 to cater to  needs of educationally unserved/ underserved areas. The scheme has 
been further extended till 31 st March, 2028. Under the Scheme, support is provided to States/UTs for 
strengthening infrastructure, including research facilities, construction of hostels, academic and 
administrative buildings, laboratories, and other facilities required for improving access and quality in 
higher education. 
 
Since the inception of the RUSA in 2013, a total of 144 projects amounting to Rs. 1431.31 crore have 
been approved to the State of Maharashtra; including approval of 61 projects under PM-USHA for an 
amount of Rs. 814.24 crore. Further, under the scheme, in the Gad chiroli–Chimur Lok Sabha 
Constituency, 6 projects for an amount of Rs. 126.98 crore have been approved including approval of 
Rs. 100 crore to Gondwana University, Gadchiroli under Multidisciplinary Education and Research 
University (MERU) component. 
 
In order to improve the quality, equity and institutional governance in Technical Education, the 
MERITE (Multidisciplinary Education and Research Improvement in Technical Education) scheme 
has been approved with a total outlay of Rs. 4200 crore for a period  from 2025-26 to 2029 -30. All 
States/UTs including Maharashtra are covered under this scheme.  
 
The UGC has undertaken several initiatives to promote digital education and implementation of the 
National Education Policy for all students including rural and tribal students; the details are as follows:- 
 SWAYAM (Study Webs of Active Learning for Young Aspiring Minds) is a programme  
initiated by the Government of India available on the SWAYAM Platform 
(www.swayam.gov.in) can be accessed by anyone who is desirous of learning, at any time, and 
from anywhere.  
 UGC M assive Open Online Course (MOOC)  Portal: Archived SWAYAM Non-Technology 
Undergraduate and Postgraduate MOOCs Courses are available on the UGC MOOCs Portal. 
 E-PG Pathshala: Non -technology postgraduate e -content is available at e -PG Pathshala 
(https://epgp.inflibnet.ac.in/) and freely accessible at one place for Students/Faculty  
Members/professionals/ lifelong learners. 

 UGC has notified the University Grants Commission (Credit Framework for Online Learning 
Courses through Study Webs of Active Learning for Young Aspiring Minds) Regulations, 2021, 
which allows universities to take up to 40% of the total courses in a semester through online 
learning via the SWAYAM platform. 
 UGC e-resource portal: The UGC e-resource portal has been integrated with the Digital Seva 
Portal (https://digitalseva.csc.gov.in), a platform operated by the Min istry of Electronics and 
Information Technology (MeitY) for the delivery of digital services in rural areas through the 
Common Service Centres (CSCs) network. Through this integration, students can access digital 
learning resources, including the UGC e -resource portal (http://www.ugceresources.in), e -
content available under UGC e -PG Pathshala, which hosts e -content in 67 postgraduate 
subjects (https://epgp.inflibnet.ac.in/), and the UGC Archived SWAYAM MOOC Portal 
(https://ugcmoocs.inflibnet.ac.in/). This i ntegration enables students in rural areas to access 
higher education e-content through CSCs, thereby improving digital connectivity and learning 
opportunities. In addition, the UGC e-resource portal also hosts 27 SWAYAM Non-Technology 
Postgraduate MOOCs, translated in eight regional languages, namely Hindi, Gujarati, Marathi, 
Bangla, Tamil, Malayalam, Kannada, and Telugu, to promote multilingual access to digital 
learning resources and support inclusive education for learners across rural regions. 
 DTH Channels (Swayam Prabha): 24/7 educational content delivered through direct -to-home 
channels, ensuring reach in remote areas. It ensures access to lectures, tutorials, and study 
materials in multiple disciplines. Available free of cost via the GSAT- 15 satellite, SWAYAM 
Prabha is especially beneficial for students in remote and underserved areas, bridging the digital 
divide and enhancing access to quality education.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
DEPARTMENT OF HIGHER EDUCATION 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2340 
ANSWERED ON 03.08.2026 
 
Mental Health of Students 
 
†2340. Shri Murari Lal Meena: 
Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that the incidents of student suicides have increased during the last few years 
and that the students suicides account for a significant proportion of the total suicide cases in the 
country, if so, the State-wise details of the last five years; 
(b) whether the Government has conducted any study on the impact of examinations, competition, 
career-related pressure, parental expectations and social stress on the mental health of students, if 
so, the major findings thereof;  
(c) whether the Government has assessed that high unemployment, question paper leaks and 
uncertainty regarding employment after completion of education are also major factors of stress 
and despair among students; and  
(d) if so, the concrete and time-bound steps being taken by the Government to reduce incidents of 
students suicides and to increase employment opportunities for the youth? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(DR. SUKANTA MAJUMDAR) 
(a) to (d): National Crime Record Bureau (NCRB) collects data on suicides from police recorded 
suicide cases. Comprehensive analysis of the data related to the accidental deaths and suicides in 
the country is published in the yearly Accidental Death & Suicide in India (ADSI) reports by 
National Crime Record Bureau (NCRB). As per ADSI Report, causes of student suicides include 
family problems, love affairs, illness, and failure in examination. Year wise, State wise, Gender and 
Age group wise details of student suicides are available in the ADSI reports which are accessible 
at https://ncrb.gov.in/accidental-deaths-suicides-in-india-year-wise.html .  
To address the issue of suicide, the Government is taking multi-pronged measures and provides 
psychological support to students, teachers and families for mental and emotional well-being to 
avoid incidences of suicide. 
National Education Policy (NEP), 2020 recognizes that education must build character and enable 
learners to become ethical, rational, compassionate, and caring individuals while preparing them 
for gainful and fulfilling employment. The Policy emphasizes holistic and multidisciplinary 
education that promotes cognitive development, character building, creativity, and key 21st century 

 
 
skills. It aims to develop well-rounded individuals with deep knowledge in their chosen fields 
alongside capabilities across a range of disciplines. NEP 2020 also underscores the importance of 
promoting student wellness through physical fitness, good health, psychosocial well-being, and 
sound ethical grounding to support high-quality learning and reduce mental stress. 
An initiative of Ministry of Education, MANODARPAN, covers a wide range of activities to 
provide psychological support to students, teachers and families for mental and emotional well-
being such as National toll-free helpline to provide guidance to callers through trained counsellor; 
live interactive sessions ‘Sahyog’ and Webinars ‘Paricharcha’ that are organized regularly to create 
awareness about the importance of mental health among all stakeholders, students in all States/UTs 
etc. These sessions are telecast on PM e-Vidya channels and are also available on ‘NCERT Official’ 
YouTube Channel. 
UGC has issued advisory to HEIs in January, 2023 circulating the National Suicide Prevention 
Strategy framed by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare. UGC also issued Guidelines on 
13.04.2023, which provide for promoting physical fitness and sports activities for students; creating 
safeguards against academic pressure, peer pressure, behavioral issues, stress, career concerns, 
depression and other issues on the mental health of students; to teach positive thinking & emotions 
in the student community; and to promote a positive and supportive network for students. 
The Ministry of Education in July, 2023 has circulated a framework guideline on emotional and 
mental well-being of students in Higher Education Institutes (HEIs) with request to take proactive 
measures to incorporate the same in the institutional functioning and instil a feeling of confidence 
in the student community. The guidelines emphasised counselling services, early distress 
identification, suicide prevention SOPs, student support networks, strengthened grievance redressal 
mechanisms, and periodic institutional review to ensure sustained effectiveness. 
Guidelines for Regulation of Coaching Centres (January 2024) has been issued by the Ministry of 
Education, which mandates student-support and protection measures such as counselling facilities, 
transparent fee structures, prohibition of batch segregation, and safeguards against practices that 
intensify academic pressure - extending mental-wellbeing protections beyond campuses. 
An Integrated approach for Promoting Positive Mental Health, Resilience, and Wellbeing has been 
conceptualized under the Malaviya Mission Teacher Training Programme. Under this integrated 
approach, two fortnightly sessions are being held with faculty of higher education institutions to 
empower them to address student mental health concerns for early intervention. Annual National 
Wellbeing Conclaves were organised at IIT Hyderabad in November, 2024 and at IIT Bombay in 
November, 2025. A Regional Workshop on Mental Health was organized on 12-13 July 2026 at 
IIT Madras, which brought together institutional leaders, faculty, students, and mental health 
professionals to share best practices and strengthen campus wellbeing ecosystems. More than 4000 
faculty have participated in online capacity building sessions, conclaves and regional workshop 
since May 2024. 
All IITs, IIMs, NITs and IIITs have put in place dedicated mental health or counselling centres 
within their campuses, staffed with full-time or visiting professional counsellors, clinical 
psychologists, and in some cases, psychiatrists. A large number of institutes often host mental health 
training sessions to raise awareness, reduce stigma, and educate students about mental health issues. 
These sessions cover topics such as stress management, coping strategies, and recognizing the signs 

 
 
of mental health issues. Some Institutes offers on/off-campus counselling services, where students 
can meet with mental health professionals. 
NEP 2020 envisages integration of skill development and vocational education with mainstream 
higher education to enhance employability, entrepreneurship and lifelong learning. AICTE is 
actively strengthening skill development by embedding it into technical education. It partners with 
industries and institutions to offer online skill courses aligned with the regular curriculum, along 
with skill-focused programmes, compulsory internships, and vocational degrees. 
To support skill development, the SWAYAM Plus portal has also been launched, focusing on 
upskilling and reskilling the workforce. More than 500 courses have been developed curated from 
89 industry partners across 17 sectors and offered on emerging areas such as AI, Data Analyst etc. 
So far, more than 6,00,000 students registered on the platform. 
The National Apprenticeship Training Scheme (NATS) bridges the gap between academic learning 
and industry requirements by providing structured on-the-job training to graduates and diploma 
holders. The Scheme promotes industry-integrated education through Apprenticeship Embedded 
Degree Programmes (AEDP), supports apprenticeships in emerging areas such as Artificial 
Intelligence (AI), and facilitates academic credit integration through the NATS Assessment and 
Creditisation Framework.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT 
LOK SABHA

TO BE ANSWERED ON 03RD AUGUST, 2026 
 
UNEMPLOYMENT RATE 
 
2341.      MS. S JOTHIMANI: 
 
Will the Minister of LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the details of unemployment rate during the last five years and the 
current year in the country, rural –urban, age, gender, year and 
State/UT-wise; 
(b) the details of major factors contributing to persistent 
unemployment especially among youth and educated jobseekers; 
(c) whether the Government has undertaken any assessment of job 
losses in key sectors and if so, the details thereof; and 
(d) the details of corrective measures taken by the Government to 
reduce unemployment? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT 
(SUSHRI SHOBHA KARANDLAJE) 
 
(a) to (d): Official estimates of employment and unemployment in India 
are derived from the Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS), conducted by 
the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation since 2017 –18. 
The PLFS methodology was revamped with effect from January 2025. 
The PLFS Annual Report 2025 is the first report in the revised series to 
present labour market estimates, covering the period from January to 
December 2025. 
 
As per latest PLFS report 2025, the estimated Unemployment Rate 
(UR) on usual status for persons of age 15 years and above was 3.6% in 
2022, 3.1% in 2023, 3.2% in 2024 and 3.1% in 2025 in the country. Also, 
the estimated UR for persons of age 15 years and above was 2.8%, 2.4%, 
2.5% and 2.4% in rural areas and 5.9%, 5.2%, 5.0% and 4.8% in urban 
areas during the same period. 
 
 
 

 
Further, the estimated UR for persons of age 15 years and above 
gender-wise in the country is as follows:

  Source : PLFS, MoSPI 
 
The estimated UR for youth of age 15 -29 years on usual status has 
decreased from 10.9% in 2022 to 9.9% in 2025 in the country and the 
estimated Unemployment Rate (UR) for educated persons of age 15 
years and above during 2025 is as follows:

Further, the estimated Worker Population Ratio (WPR) indicating 
employment on usual status for persons of age 15 years and above has 
increased from 54.1% in 2022 to 57.4% in 2025 in the country. 
 
Year-wise, sector -wise, gender -wise, area -wise & State/UT -wise 
information is available in the PLFS reports which may be seen at the 
website of MoSPI at https://www.mospi.gov.in/publications-reports. 
Employment generation coupled with improving employability for 
youth is a priority of the Government. Accordingly, Government is 
implementing various employment generation schemes/ programmes in 
the country (including for rural youth). The details of various employment 
generation schemes/ programmes being implemented by the Government 
may be seen at   https://dge.gov.in/dge/schemes_programmes. 
 
 
 

 
Additionally, Government is also implementing Skill India Mission 
(SIM) to deliver skill, re -skill and up -skill training through an extensive 
network of skill development centres/ schools/ colleges /institutes etc. 
under various schemes, viz. Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana 
(PMKVY), Jan Shikshan Sansthan (JSS), National Apprenticeship 
Promotion Scheme (NAPS) and Craftsmen Training Scheme (CTS) 
through Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs) in the country. The SIM aims 
at enabling youth of India to get future ready, equipped with industry 
relevant skills. 
 
The Ministry of MSME launched Udyam Registration Portal on 
01.07.2020 for formalizing enterprises, expanding access to government 
support and strengthening the MSME ecosystem. A total of 8.9 crore 
Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) have been registered on 
Udyam Registration Portal, including Udyam Assist Platform (UAP), 
providing employment to over 39 crore people across the country. 
 
Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) has 
initiated ‘FutureSkills PRIME’ a programme for Re -skilling/Up-skilling of 
IT Manpower for Employability in 10 new/emerging technologies 
including Artificial Intelligence. 
 
Also, the Government is implementing Employment Linked 
Incentive (ELI) Scheme named as the Pradhan Mantri Viksit Bharat 
Rozgar Yojana to support employment generation, enhance employability 
and social security across all sectors, with special focus on the 
manufacturing sector. The scheme with an outlay of Rs 99,446 Crore 
aims to incentivize the creation of more than 3.5 Crore jobs in the 
country, over a period of 2 years.  
 
Further, Ministry of Labour and Employment, Government of India, 
is running the National Career Service (NCS) Portal which is a one -stop 
solution for providing career related services including jobs from private 
and government sectors, information on online & offline job fairs, job 
search & matching, career counselling, vocational guidance, information 
on skill development courses, skill/training programmes etc. through a 
digital platform [www.ncs.gov.in].

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF EDUCATION

LOK SABHA  
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO-2342  
ANSWERED ON-03/08/2026 
 
PM Research Chair Scheme in Andhra Pradesh 
 
2342. Shri Magunta Sreenivasulu Reddy: 
 
Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the number of applications received and researchers selected under the PM Research Chair 
Scheme since its inception, year-wise, State-wise and district-wise for Andhra Pradesh; 
(b) whether any researchers from Andhra Pradesh have applied or been selected under the said 
Scheme and if so, the details thereof; 
(c) whether any institutions in Andhra Pradesh have been selected as host institutions under 
the said Scheme and if so, the details regarding the list of such institutions; 
(d) the steps being taken by the Government to encourage more Indian -origin researchers, 
particularly from the Telugu States, to return and contribute to India's research and innovation; 
and 
(e) the details of funds allocated and utilized for awareness creation of the scheme, State-wise, 
especially for Andhra Pradesh? 
 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(DR. SUKANTA MAJUMDAR) 
 
(a) to (e): The Government of India has framed and approved the National Education Policy 
(NEP) 2020 to transform the education landscape into a multidisciplinary, inclusive, and 
learner-centric ecosystem. The Policy aims to enhance equity, quality and access to education 
for all, while promoting research and innovation as key components of higher education. 
 
In pursuance with the vision of NEP 2020, the Ministry of Education has launched the Prime 
Minister Research Chair (PMRC) Scheme to attract and engage distinguished Indian-origin 
researchers, scientists and professionals with international research experience , to strengthen 
India's higher education and research ecosystem through research, mentorship and institutional 
capacity-building across national priority thematic areas. The Scheme provides for fellowships 
under three categories, namely Research Chair, Senior Fellow and Young Research Fellow. 
 
Applications have been invited from eligible candidates for fellowships. Applications have also 
been invited from eligible institutions to participate in the PMRC Scheme as host institutions. 
These institutions are spread across various States/ UTs of India to engage top Indian origin 
researchers for their research projects aligned with identified thematic areas.  

 
To ensure wider outreach of the Scheme, the Ministry of Education in collaboration with the 
Indian Embassies/ High Commissions has taken steps for awareness of the Scheme among 
eligible candidates. Details of scheme, eligibility criteria for fellows  and host institutions are 
available at https://pmrc.education.gov.in/ .  
 
Further, Ministry of Science and Technology has formulated several schemes to encourage 
Indian-origin researchers to return and contribute to India’s research and innovation  which 
includes INSPIRE and V AIBHA V . The INSPIRE (Innovation in Science Pursuit for Inspired 
Research) Faculty Scheme provides attractive avenues and opportunities to Indian researchers, 
who are residing in foreign, to work in Indian Institutes/Universities in their respective domain, 
whereas V AIBHA V (Vaishvik Bharatiya Vaigyanik) is a Fellowship Programme exclusively 
for Indian Diaspora (Non-Resident Indian/ Overseas Citizen of India), these fellows have been 
hosted by various Indian Institutions including IIT Hyderabad. 
 
Further, Anusandhan National Research Foundation (ANRF) under Department of Science and 
Technology has also formulated the RAMANUJAN fellowship scheme to engage  brilliant 
Indian/Indian-Origin scientists and researchers working abroad to pursue research in Indian 
universities, academic institutions, National laboratories and across all disciplines of science 
and engineering. The support to fellows includes a consolidated fellowship of ₹1.35 lakh per 
month, along with a research grant of ₹7 lakh per annum for a period of five years.

(a) whether it is a fact that school drop out rates in the country saw a notable decline in the 2025 -26 
academic year, according to the official UDISE+ (unified district information system for education plus) 
in the country, if so, the details thereof; 
(b) the details of policy adopted by Government in expanding access to education,  strengthening school 
infrastructure, improving teacher availability and reducing school drop-out in the country; 
(c) whether it is a fact that being one of the largest school education systems in the world the Government 
proposes to develop residential schools in the country specially for the students of remote village areas, if 
so, the details thereof for West-Bengal; and 
(d) the details of proposal and act ion taken by the Government to develop and abolish the existing 
significant inter-State and wide regional disparities regarding use of modern technology and smart tuition 
facilities in the country particularly in the States of West Bengal, Meghalaya, Aruna chal Pradesh, Bihar 
and Manipur having limiting equitable access to digital learning opportunities? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(SHRI JAYANT CHAUDHARY) 
 
(a): As per Unified District Information System for Education Plus (UDISE+), the dropout rate during 
2024-25 and 2025-26 at various educational stages are as under:  
 
Year Preparatory (class 
III to class V) 
Middle (class VI to 
class VIII) 
Secondary (class IX 
to XII) 
2024-25 2.3 3.5 8.2 
2025-26 1.8 3.6 7.0 
 
 
(b) and (c): Under the Centrally Sponsored schemes like Samagra Shiksha, STARS and PM SHRI, 
States/UTs are supported for strengthening of existing government schools, and for creation and 
augmentation of infrastructure facilities like Additional Classrooms, Toilets for Boys/Girls/CWSN, 
Drinking Water, Electricity, Boundary Walls, Library, ICT and Digital Classrooms, based on the gaps 
determined from Unified District Information System for Education plus (UDISE+) database and 
proposals received from respective State/U T. The requirement of infrastructural facilities in schools is 
worked out every year by the respective State/UT on incremental basis depending on their need and 
priority and reflected in their Annual Work Plan and Budget (AWP&B). These plans are then appra ised 
and approved by Project Approval Board (PAB) in consultation with the States /UTs as per the 
programmatic and financial norms of the scheme, physical and financial progress of works sanctioned 
earlier and availability of budgetary resources.  Also, The Central Government assist  States and UTs 

through the Centrally Sponsored Scheme of Samagra Shiksha and hot cooked meal provided from 
Balvatika to class 8 under Pradhan Mantri Poshan Shakti Nirman (PM POSHAN) Yojna.  
   Financial assistance/grant is also pr ovided to the States and UTs  including West Bengal  for 
various activities to reduce dropout and increase enrolment in Government schools, which include 
opening/strengthening of new schools up to Senior Secondary level, strengthening school infrastructure, 
setting up and up gradation and running of Kasturba Gandhi Balika Vidyalayas (KGBV) upto class 12, 
setting up of residential schools/hostels named Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose Avasiya Vidyalayas, hostels 
under Pradhan Mantri Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha Abhiya n (PM-JANMAN) and Dharti Aaba Janjatiya 
Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan (DAJGUA), transport allowance, undertaking enrolment drives, seasonal 
hostels/residential camps, provision of skill education and ICT facilities in schools, providing free text 
books and free uniform, transport/escort facility, etc. 
 
PM SHRI Scheme has also been launched with an aim to develop more than 14,500 selected 
schools as exemplar schools that offer leadership to other schools in the neighbourhood, showcasing all 
the initiatives of NEP 2020 
 
Education being a subject in the Concurrent List of the Constitution, an overwhelming majority of 
the schools in the country comes under the administrative control of States/UTs. The recruitment, service 
conditions and rational deployment of teachers fa ll under the purview of the respective State 
Governments/UT Administrations. Recruitment of teachers is a continuous process, and vacancies arise 
on account of various factors such as retirement, resignation and increased requirement of teachers due to 
growth in student enrolment. The Central Government through the Centrally Sponsored Scheme of 
Samagra Shiksha, provides financial assistance to the States and UTs to maintain appropriate Pupil -
Teacher Ratio (PTR) for various levels of schooling, as per norms prescribed in the Right of Children to 
Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act, 2009, as amended from time to time. 
 
(d): A comprehensive initiative called PM eVidya was initiated as part of 'Atmanirbhar Bharat 
Abhiyaan' on 17th May, 2020, which unifies al l efforts related to digital/online/on -air education to 
enable multi -mode access to education across the country  including the states of West Bengal, 
Meghalaya, Arunachal Pradesh, Bihar and Manipur  under the aegis of National Education Policy 
(NEP) 2020. States/Union Territories (UTs) collaborate with NCERT to utilise, monitor and evaluate 
the effectiveness of these initiatives as per their requirements in mother tongue/local/regional 
languages. PM eVidya includes 200 DTH TV Channels allotted to  States/UTs/Autonomous Bodies 
(ABs)/Other Ministries in Government of India and 400 Radio channels to enable them to provide 
supplementary education as per their requirement in various Indian languages for classes 1-12. 
 
Digital Infrastructure for Knowledge Sharing (DIKSHA) is the Nation's One Nation, One 
Digital platform for providing quality e -content for school education in States/UTs along with QR 
coded Energised Textbooks (ETBs) for all grades. States/UTs/ ABs have generated and contributed 
over 3.7 lakh content in mother local/regional languages enabling multilingualism. DIKSHA Offline 
supports areas with limited or no internet connectivity. The stakeholders have access to more than 450+ 
Virtual Labs and 100 Virtual skill labs on DIKSHA.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2346 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 03.08.2026 
 
Environmental Clearance for Handling of Coal/Coke 
 
2346.  SHRI CAPTAIN VIRIATO FERNANDES: 
Will the Minister of Environment, Forest and Climate Change be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether handling of coal/coke at a Mooring Dolphin forming part of an existing Major 
Port situated within the Coastal Regulation Zone (CRZ) requires prior Environmental 
Clearance under the Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) Notification, 2006, if so, the 
details thereof;  
(b) whether commencement of cargo handling operations at a new berth, jetty, mooring 
dolphin or similar facility within an existing port also requires prior Environmental Clearance, 
irrespective of whether the port already possesses an Environmental Clearance for other 
facilities, if so, the details thereof;  
(c) whether the Government has granted any Environmental Clearance specifically 
permitting coal/coke handling at the Mooring Dolphins of the Mormugao Port Authority, Goa 
and if so, the details thereof;  
(d) if not, whether such operations would amount to a violation of the Environment 
(Protection) Act, 1986 and the EIA Notification, 2006; and  
(e) if so, the action taken by the Government thereon? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND 
CLIMATE CHANGE 
 (SHRI KIRTI VARDHAN SINGH) 
 
(a) to  (e) The Government of India has issued Environment Impact Assessment (EIA) 
Notification, 2006 under the powers conferred by sub-section (1) and clause (v) of sub-section 
(2) of section 3 of the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986. As per the provision of EIA 
Notification, 2006, construction of new projects or  activities or  the expansion or 
modernization of existing projects or activities listed in the Schedule to this notification  
entailing capacity addition with change in process and/or technology shall be undertaken in 
any part of India only after the prior environmental clearance from the Central Government or 
as the case may be, by the State Level Environment Impact Assessment Authority, duly 
constituted by the Central Government under sub-section (3) of section 3 of the said Act, in 
accordance with the procedure specified in the EIA Notification. In so far as appraisal of a 
project from the environmental perspective is concerned, prior assessment of environmental 

impacts and risk forms the basis for grant of Environmental Clearance. The project is rigorously 
appraised by an independent Expert Appraisal Committee (EAC), which examines its 
components, cargo type and capacity, berth capacity and handling facilities, environmental 
impacts, risk assessment and mitigation measures, and may prescribe additional project-
specific conditions. Based on the EAC's recommendations, the Ministry of Environment, 
Forest and Climate Change grants Environmental Clearance subject to specific and general 
terms and conditions. Any project or activity undertaken in violation of the provisions of the 
EIA Notification, 2006 attracts the penal provisions under Section 15 of the Environment 
(Protection) Act, 1986, and the rules made thereunder. 
 
The operation of projects or activities is regulated under the provisions of the Water 
(Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974 and the Air (Prevention and Control of 
Pollution) Act, 1981. Accordingly, no industry, operation or process shall commence or 
continue its operation without obtaining a valid Consent to Operate (CTO) from the concerned 
State Pollution Control Board (SPCB) or Pollution Control Committee (PCC), as applicable. 
 
The Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change has granted following 
Environmental and CRZ clearance in favour of Mormugao Port Authority, Goa 
 
(i) Terminal capacity enhancement at Berth 5A-6A for coal and coal products, Iron Ore and 
Limestone including unitised and steel products vide letter dated 11.01.2023,  
(ii) Redevelopment of berths 8, 9 and barge berth vide letter dated 06.07.2023 and  
(iii) Deepening of approach channel for capsize vessel vide letter dated 21.07.2025.  
As per the information provided by the Mormugao Port Authority, they have obtained Consent 
to Operate (CTO) from the Goa State Pollution Control Board for handling various categories 
of cargo, including dry bulk cargo, break bulk cargo, coal and coke, at Mooring Dolphins 1, 2 
and 3. However, no Consent to Operate has been issued by the Goa State Pollution Control 
Board in respect of Mooring Dolphins 4, 5 and 6, and accordingly, these facilities remain 
unutilized.

Will the Minister of TOURISM be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the details of the Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) being used to 
evaluate the success of completed sustainable tourism infrastructure 
projects under various central tourism schemes, including parameters 
relating to tourist footfall, employment generation , local income, 
environmental sustainability and visitor satisfaction across the country,

Nathdwara, Kumbhalghar and Udaipur and its nearby areas and 
Nabarangpur Lok Sabha Constituency, including Deobrahmani Temp le 
(Paparahandi), Tentasikundi, Chandan Dhara Waterfall, Balimela 
Reservoir, Satiguda Dam and Amakunda; 
(b) the details of the mechanisms in place to involve indigenous, local 
community leaders, local self -government institutions, traditional 
leaders and other stakeholders during the planning and implementation 
of destination development projects especially in t he said tourist 

destinations in Nabarangpur  and Malkangiri districts and tribal and 
aspirational districts such as Kalahandi; 
(c) whether the Government has established any institutional mechanism to 
periodically assess the economic impact, tourist footfall and 
employment generation arising from the major tourist destinations in 
Nabarangpur and Malkangiri districts and Sidhi Lok Sabha Constituency;

development, promotion and tourism infrastructure of the said tourist 
destinations; and

destinations in Kalahandi district of Odisha and if so, the details thereof 
along with the measures proposed to promote its rich tribal, cultural, 
archaeological and eco -tourism potential und er central tourism 
schemes? 
ANSWER

concerned State Government (SG)/UT Administration (UTA). However, Ministry 
of Tourism under its various schemes such as Swadesh Darshan (SD), 
Swadesh Darshan 2.0 (SD2.0), Challenge Based Destina tion Development 
(CBDD) – an initiative under Swadesh Darshan and Pilgrimage Rejuvenation 
and Spiritual Heritage Augmentation Drive (PRASHAD) etc. provides financial 
assistance for development of tourism infrastructure and experiences in the 
country, to th e SGs/UTAs, on receipt of the project proposals from them, in 
synergy with the scheme guidelines, Government directions, availability of 
funds, inter-se priority etc. 
 
Government of India under its ‘Special Assistance to States for Capital 
Investment (SASCI) – Development of Iconic Tourist Centres to Global Scale’ 
has also sanctioned multiple projects in 2024-25 with the primary objective to 
comprehensively develop iconi c tourist centres in the country, branding and 
marketing them at global scale. 
 
Further, the projects sanctioned under the above schemes are regularly 
monitored at various levels. The Guidelines for Swadesh Darshan 2.0, includes 
National Institutional Framework comprising of Central Sanctioning and 
Monitoring Committee (CSMC), Mission  Directorate (MD) etc., State 
Institutional Framework and Destination Management Committees are to be 

set up by the State Governments/UTAs. The Ministry has also developed a 
Program Management Information System (PMIS) for monitoring of its 
destination development related schemes as a unified digital platform to 
facilitate seamless information, communication, sharing and reporting system 
in respect of the projects undertaken as part of its various schemes. Ministry 
of Tourism and SGs/UTAs including project implementing agencies are integral 
part of this system.

submitted under Swadesh Darshan 2.0 scheme to include current and project 
tourist footfall in the destination, direct and indirect employment to be 
generated at the project site and potential  revenue sources from the project 
to meet operation and maintenance costs of the projects upon completion.

destinations are considered for sanctioning, as per project requirement 
including those related to tourism core products, tourism activities, safety, 
sanitation, last mile connectivity, pa rking, general site development, soft 
interventions like digitization, skilling etc.  
 
No proposal is under consideration with Ministry of tourism for 
development of Nabarangpur, Malkangiri and Kalahandi districts.

Government of India

Declining Competitiveness of Indian Football 
 
2350.          SHRI JAI PRAKASH: 
 
Will the Minister of YOUTH AFFAIRS AND SPORTS be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government has undertaken any assessment of the 
reasons for India’s declining performance in the international 
football, including its FIFA ranking and performance in major  
international and continental tournaments during the last three years 
and the current year; 
  
(b) if so, whether the Government has evaluated the effectiveness of 
existing schemes for football development, including grassroots 
talent identification, coach ing standards, sports science support, 
infrastructure development and participation in domestic leagues; 
  
(c) if so, whether the Government proposes to formulate a long -term 
National Football Development Strategy in collaboration with State 
Governments, e ducational institutions and football associations, 
including the FIFA World Cup and the AFC Asian Cup; and 
  
(d) if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF YOUTH AFFAIRS AND SPORTS 
[DR. MANSUKH MANDAVIYA] 
  
(a) to (d):    Promotion and development of a specific sport discipline 
is the responsibility of the concerned National Sports Federation 
(NSF), which in the case of football is the All India Football Federation 
(AIFF).  

Page 2 of 3 
 
The Ministry of Youth Affairs & Sports has recognised the AIFF as 
NSF for the promotion and development of football in the country. 
  
Rankings of football teams are dynamic and influenced by match 
results, strength of opposition, and frequency of matches. The Sports 
Authority of India (SAI), an autonomous body under the aegis of the 
Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports, regularly engages with the AIFF 
to review the performance and overall development of the sport and 
provides its advice accordingly. 
  
Under the Scheme of Assistance to NSFs, the AIFF is being provided 
with financial assistance towards training of athletes, which includes 
all requisite facilities for their preparations including wholesome 
nutritious diet, food supplements, equipment support, state-of-the-art 
infrastructure, lodging, travelling facilities, services of reputed Indian 
and Foreign Coaches/ supporting staff, scientific & medical support, 
sports kit, etc. besides financial assistance for their training abroad 
and conduct of national championships in Sub Junior, Junior and 
Senior Categories, conduct of inter national tournaments in India, 
participation in international competitions in India and abroad. For 
the said purpose, an ACTC (Annual Calendar for Training and 
Competition) budget is approved for each NSF, including the AIFF, 
every year. 
  
The norms under the Scheme of Assistance to NSFs have been 
revised on 22.05.2025. The scheme ensures robust grassroots 
development, professional coaching, scientific support to athletes, 
and increased exposure through support to NSFs for hosting and 
participation in inter national sporting events. It also prioritizes 
grassroot development and capacity building of coaches and 
technical staff. 
  
Apart from above, the following measures have been undertaken: 
  
i. The football has been supported by inclusion in Khelo  India 
Youth Games and promoting talent through Khelo India 
Academies and State Centres of Excellence.  
ii. Facilitating infrastructure and sports science support at 
National Centres of Excellence.  

Page 3 of 3 
 
  
Further, SAI through its various sports promotional schemes , 
encourages the sports of football, across the country, to identify 
talented sportspersons in the various age groups and nurture them to 
excel at national and international levels.
