GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2379 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 03.08.2026 
CLIMATE RESILIENCE AND SOCIAL SECURITY FOR VULNERABLE 
WORKERS 
 
2379. SHRI MADDILA GURUMOORTHY: 
 
Will the Minister of LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT be pleased to 
state:  
 
(a)whether the impact of extreme weather events, including heavy 
rainfall and flooding on informal and daily -wage workers has been 
assessed and if so, the details thereof; 
(b)whether any nat ional guidelines exist to protect workers whose 
livelihoods are disrupted due to adverse climatic conditions and if so, 
the details thereof; 
(c)whether social security mechanisms are available for workers 
affected by weather related work interruptions and if so, the details 
thereof; and 
(d)whether the Government proposes to formulate a climate resilience 
framework for vulnerable workers and if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT 
(SUSHRI SHOBHA KARANDLAJE) 
 
(a) to (d): The Government of India has been monitoring and recording 
the occurrence of various extreme weather events, including heavy 
rainfall and flooding, heat waves, cyclones, etc. across the country.  
 
 Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change has  initiated 
the preparation of India's National Adaptation Plan (NAP) on Climate 
Change, which aims to build resilience and reduce vulnerability to 
climate-related risks across sectors including agriculture, water and 
biodiversity. 
 
  Ministry of Labour and  Employment issues Nationwide 
Heatwave Advisory to protect workers and labourers. The Ministry also 
issues advisories to all States/UTs and its attached organisations, 
urging immediate preventive and mitigation measures to safeguard 
workers and labourers f rom the adverse effects of rising temperatures 
and heat wave conditions across the country. 
Contd..2/- 
 

:: 2 :: 
  Further, the India Meteorological Department, in 
collaboration with various research centers across the country, has 
undertaken several initiatives to enhance monitoring and early warning 
systems across the country, including urban climate platforms. These 
efforts have significantly contributed to minimizing the loss of life and 
property during extreme weather events, including heat waves. These  
include: 
• Heat Action Plans (HAPs) in 23 States that are prone to heatwave 
conditions were jointly implemented by the National Disaster 
Management Authority (NDMA) in collaboration with the State 
Governments. 
• Issuing seasonal and monthly outlooks, followed  by extended -
range forecasts of temperature and heatwave conditions. The 
early warning and forecast information are also disseminated 
through various social media platforms for timely public outreach. 
• District-wise heatwave vulnerability Atlas over India to help State 
Government authorities and disaster management agencies in 
planning. 
• The hot weather hazard analysis map of India incorporates daily 
data on temperature, wind patterns, and humidity levels. 
• A series of National and State -level heatwave prepare dness 
meetings are conducted much before the start of the summer 
season, with regular review meetings from time to time during the 
season. 
 
  The Disaster Management Act, 2005 provides for the legal 
and institutional framework for the effective management of disasters. 
National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA) has prepared the 
National Disaster Management Plan (NDMP) in 2016 the updated and 
revised it in 2019. NDMP provides a framework and direction to the 
government agencies for all phases of disaster management cycle. It is 
a strategic tool in further strengthening disaster resilient development 
in the country. 
 
  The primary responsibility for disaster management 
including disbursal of relief assistance on ground level rests with the 
State Governments concerned. The Central Government provides 
requisite logistics and financial assistance to support the efforts of the 
State Governments. 
  The State Governments provide financial relief to the 
affected people in the event of 12 notified natural  disasters, which 
includes floods and landslides, from the State Disaster Response Fund 
(SDRF), already placed at its disposal in accordance with approved 
items and norms of Government of India.

†2380. SMT. SHOBHANABEN MAHENDRASINH BARAIYA:  
            SHRI BHOJRAJ NAG: 
            SHRI ARVIND DHARMAPURI: 
            SHRI ANURAG SINGH THAKUR:

            SHRI ANIL FIROJIYA: 
    DR. LATA WANKHEDE:  
 
Will the Minister of YOUTH AFFAIRS AND SPORTS be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the current status of the Target Olympia Podium Scheme (TOPS), 
including the number of athletes supported under the core and 
development groups along with the number of talented athletes under 
TOPS, Khelo India, ASMITA and other Sports Authority of India 
programme, State/UT/district and Constituency-wise and sports-wise 
including Chhattisgarh and Kanker region, Telangana (particularly 
Nizamabad and Jagtial district) and Dewas -Shajapur Lok Sabha 
Constituency in Madhya Pradesh; 
 
(b) the details of financial assistance,  sports science support, 
international exposure, coaching and other assistance being 
provided to the athletes under TOPS and Khelo India Schemes from 
the said State/UT/district and Constituency;  
 
(c) the details of measures taken to strengthen the partici pation of 
women, rural and tribal sportspersons and para -athletes through 
initiatives such as ASMITA, Khelo India centre and Sports Authority 
of India (SAI) training centres in the said State/UT/district and 
Constituency; 
 

Page 2 of 19 
 
(d) whether the Government has formulated a long-term roadmap to 
expand high  performance support, athlete welfare and talent 
development for 2032 and 2036 Olympic Games in the country; and 
 
(e) if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF YOUTH AFFAIRS & SPORTS 
[DR. MANSUKH MANDAVIYA] 
 
(a) to  (c): TOPS is the Government's flagship programme for 
enhancing India's medal prospects at the Olympic and Paralympic 
Games. Details of elite sportspersons supported under TOPS are at 
Annexure-I, while the list of 62 para-athletes inducted under TOPS is 
at Annexure-II. 
 
During the current session, 90 para -athletes have been inducted 
under the Khelo India Scheme. Para Sports are being supported 
through the following Nationa l Centres of Excellence (NCOEs) the 
details of which are attached at Annexure-VII. 
 
A total of 2,786 athletes are supported under the Khelo India Scheme. 
State-wise details are at Annexure -III, discipline -wise details at 
Annexure-IV, and district-wise details are available on the Khelo India 
dashboard at https://dashboard.kheloindia.gov.in/khelo-india-center-
dashboard. 
Further, the Sports Authority of India (SAI) implements the NCOEs, 
SAI Training Centres (STCs) including Extension Centres, and 
National Sports Talent Contest (NSTC), including Adopted Akharas, 
for identification and development of sporting talent. The 
sanctioned strength is 4,384 athletes under NCOEs and 4,824 
athletes under STCs. State-wise details for Chhattisgarh, Telangana 
and Madhya Pradesh are at Annexure -V, while financial assistance 
under various SAI Schemes is at Annexure -VI. 
Further, 174 Khelo India Centres (KICs) are operational across 174 
priority tribal districts, supporting 647 female and 664 male 
athletes. 

Page 3 of 19 
 
To promote women's participation in sports, the Khelo India ASMITA 
League, launched in 2021, has conducted over 3,500 leagues across 
700 cities in 38 disciplines, with participation of over 6 lakh women 
athletes. Additionally, over 450 ASMITA leagues have been 
conducted across 170 tribal districts in 30 States/UTs, covering 32 
disciplines. 
Selection of athletes, including women, rural, tribal and para -
athletes, for competitions is the prerogative of the concerned 
National Sports Federation (NSF) as per its selection p olicy. 
Under TOPS, para-athletes in the Core Group receive a monthly Out -
of-Pocket Allowance (OPA) of ₹50,000, while the identified Khelo 
India Athletes receive ₹10,000 per month  under Khelo India 
Scheme. 
(d) and (e): The Government has adopted a comprehensive approach 
to improve India's performance in major international sporting 
events, including the Olympic Games, through talent identification, 
world-class coaching and training, modern sports infrastructure, 
sports s cience and medical support, international exposure, and 
financial assistance under schemes such as TOPS, Assistance to 
NSFs, Khelo India, and NCOEs.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2381 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 03.08.2026 
WORKER SAFETY AND WELFARE MEASURES 
 
2381. SHRI SHYAMKUMAR DAULAT BARVE: 
 
Will the Minister of LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT be pleased to 
state:  
 
(a)the details of welfare, health and safety facilities mandated by law 
to be provided to  workers including contract, migrant and gig 
workers, along with safety training, medical facilities,  safety 
equipment, shelter, insurance and any other facilities mandated to 
be provided thereof; 
(b)whether the Government has conducted any assessment to find 
out whether the said facilities have been provided by the employers 
and establishments; 
(c)if so,  the details of establishments/industries etc. found to be 
complying and non-complying to the said statutory mandate; 
(d) whether the Government has carried out any assessment to find 
out the facilities provided  or mandated for the safety of workers 
including contract, migrant and gig workers are adequate  or not 
and if so, the details thereof; and 
(e)whether the Government has proposed any policy or measure to 
improve the compliance  of the said mandates so as to reduce 
industrial accidents, injuries and dea ths and if so, the  details 
thereof? 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT 
(SUSHRI SHOBHA KARANDLAJE) 
 
(a) to (e): The Government has enacted Occupational Safety, 
Health and Working Conditions (OSH&WC) Code 2020, which came 
into force from 21.11.2025, to regulate safety, health and working 
conditions of the persons employed including contract and migrant 
worker in an e stablishment and for matters connected therewith 
or incidental thereto.  The Central Government has notified OSH & 
WC (Central) Rules 2026 on 08.05.2026. There are elaborate 
provisions pertaining to occupational safety, health, welfare, 
penalties and procedures etc. under the OSH & WC Code 2020 and 
rules framed thereunder.   
Contd..2/- 

:: 2 :: 
  The OSH & WC Code 2020 empowers the employer is to 
ensure that workplace is free from hazards which cause or are 
likely to cause injury or occupational disease.  Fu rther, under the 
OSH & WC (Central) Rules 2026, there are detailed provisions 
regarding welfare provisions viz. drinking water, canteen facility, 
toilets, shelter and rest rooms, etc. The Rule also prescribed free 
annual health examination for employee who  has completed forty 
years of age in certain establishments.  
  The owner or occupier or employer, as the case may be, 
are required to comply with the provisions of the OSH & WC Code 
2020 and rules framed thereunder.  In case of factories, the OSH 
& WC Code 2020 and the rules framed thereunder are enforced by 
respective States / Union Territories. The Chief Inspector cum 
Facilitator/Inspector cum Facilitator, notified under the OSH & WC 
Code 2020, is empowered to initiate legal action against the 
occupier or employer or owner in case of violations of provisions 
of the Code or rules framed thereunder.  
      The definition of ‘gig workers’ has been provided in the 
Code on Social Security (CoSS), 2020. Gig workers are outside the 
traditional employer-employee relationship. The CoSS provides for 
framing of suitable social security  measures for gig workers and 
platform workers on matters relating to life and disability cover, 
accident insurance, health and maternity benefits, old age 
protection, etc. The Code pro vides for setting up of a Social 
Security Fund to finance these welfare schemes. The Code also 
has provisions to constitute a National Social Security Board for 
the purposes of the welfare of gig workers.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF CORPORATE AFFAIRS 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2382 
ANSWERED ON MONDAY, AUGUST 03, 2026/SHRAVANA 12, 1948 (SAKA) 
 
CSR EXPENDITURE BY CPSUs 
Question 
 
2382. Shri Kodikunnil Suresh: 
Will the Minister of CORPORATE AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the details of the donor Central Public Sector Undertakings (CPSUs) and recipient 
organisations/institutions, along with the amount sanctioned, amount released, purpose of 
them project and district-wise location of the beneficiaries; 
 
(b) the details of the officers designated to coordinate or administer CSR activities in each 
CPSU, including their official designation, office address, telephone number and official e -
mail address; 
 
(c) whether the Government maintains a centralized database of CSR projects undertaken 
by CPSUs and, if so, the details thereof; and 
 
(d) the steps taken by the Government to ensure transpare ncy, equitable distribution and 
effective monitoring of CSR funds across all States and Union Territories?  
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CORPORATE AFFAIRS AND MINISTER OF STATE 
IN THE MINISTRY OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
                                                                                      [SHRI HARSH MALHOTRA] 
 
(a): There is no provision of sanctioned/released Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) fund 
under the Companies Act, 2013. O n the basis of annual filings made by compa nies in the 
MCA21 registry, the State-wise and Development sector-wise CSR expenditure by PSUs in 
the last three Financial Years i.e. FY 2022 -23 to FY 2024-25 is attached at Annexure-I & II 
respectively. Further, beneficiary-wise data is not maintained centrally. 
(b): The details of the officers designated to coordinate or administer CSR activities is not 
maintained by the Ministry centrally. 
(c): Yes Sir. All data related to Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) filed by companies in 
MCA21 registry including PSU wise, state -wise, development sector -wise, company-wise, 
project wise and year -wise is available in public domain and can be accessed at 
www.csr.gov.in. 
 
(d): The existing legal provisions for formation of CSR committee, formulation of CSR policy, 
Annual Action Plan on CSR, identification of the project and area in which project will be   
 
Contd…2. 
 

 
-2- 
 
 
implemented, certification of CSR expenditure by Chief Financial Officer (CFO) and audit of 
CSR expenditure by statutory auditors etc. are the mechanisms to ensure transparency and 
accountability. The Board has to ensure that the approved amount has been spent on the 
assigned activity(ies).  
 
 
Under the Companies Act 2013, CSR is a Board driven process and the Board of the 
company is empowered to plan, decide, execute and monitor CSR activities of the company 
based on the recommendation of its CSR Committee. This Committee formulates and 
recommends the CSR policy, which outlines the activities to be undertaken by the company

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2383 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 03.08.2026 
 
Financial Assistance to Etawah Safari Park 
 
2383. SHRI JITENDRA KUMAR DOHARE:  
 
Will the Minister of ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE be pleased to state:  
 
(a) whether the Government is providing any financial assistance for the maintenance, 
infrastructure development, and wildlife conservation of the Etawah Safari Park, if so, 
the details thereof;  
(b) the details of funds allocated and released to this Safari Park through the Central Zoo 
Authority (CZA) or other Central Schemes during the last three years, year-wise; 
(c) whether any new proposal has been received from the State Government of Uttar Pradesh 
seeking financial aid for the expansion of the Etawah Safari Park or for the 
translocation/induction of new animals (such as lions, cheetahs, etc.); and  
(d) if so, the action taken by the Government on this proposal and the amount of funds 
proposed to be sanctioned for the purpose? 
 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND 
CLIMATE CHANGE  
(SHRI KIRTI VARDHAN SINGH) 
 
(a) to (d) The Lion Breeding Centre and Multiple Safari, Etawah is a zoo recognized by 
the Central Zoo Authority. Under the Recognition of Zoo Rules, 2009, the zoo 
operator is primarily responsible for provisioning of funds for the maintenance, 
infrastructure development and wildlife conservation of the zoo. 
 
The Central Zoo Authority provides financial assistance to recognized zoos in 
accordance with the Guidelines for Prioritizing Grant of Financial Assistance to 
Zoos (2012), based on the proposals received from the concerned zoos and 
subject to availability of budget. 
 
During 2024-25, based on the proposal received from the Lion Breeding Centre 
and multiple Safari Park, Etawah, Uttar Pradesh, an amount of Rs 23.00 lakhs 
was released by the Central Zoo Authority. However, proposals from the State of 
Uttar Pradesh for the years 2023-24 and 2025-26 including for expansion of the 
Etawah Safari Park or for the translocation/induction of new animals (such as 
lions, cheetahs, etc.) have not been received in the Central Zoo Authority.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
DEPARTMENT OF HIGHER EDUCATION 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2384 
ANSWERED ON- 03/08/2026 
 
Implementation of Pradhan Mantri Vidyalaxmi Scheme in Andhra Pradesh 
 
2384. Shri Tangella Uday Srinivas: 
          Shri B K Parthasarathi: 
Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state: 
a) the number of students who have availed education loans and interest subvention benefits under 
the Pradhan Mantri Vidyalaxmi Scheme since its inception, year -wise and Sta te/UT-wise, 
along with district, category and gender-wise details for Andhra Pradesh, especially Kakinada; 
b) the details of funds sanctioned, released and utilised during current and last financial years, 
year/State-wise, along with district-wise details for Andhra Pradesh including Kakinada; 
c) the number of beneficiaries who opted for redemption of e -voucher and number to whom 
interest subsidy has been disbursed, State-wise and district-wise for Andhra Pradesh; 
d) the number of loans wherein credit guarantee has been provided, State-wise and district-wise 
for Andhra Pradesh along with the number of exercises or audits conducted by the Government 
to ensure that correct and timely information is provided by the Leading Banks and students; 
e) whether the Government main tains a centralised record of education loans of Public Sector 
Banks classified as NPAs during the last five years and if so, the details thereof, State-wise and 
year-wise; 
f) the number of grievances filed, resolved and pending on the Vidyalaxmi  portal, State-wise 
including Andhra Pradesh, along with reasons for pendency; and 
g) whether banks are meeting prescribed processing timelines on the Vidyalaxmi portal and if not, 
the corrective steps taken by the Government thereon? 
ANSWER 
  
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(DR. SUKANTA MAJUMDAR) 
 
(a) to (g) The Government of India has launched the PM-Vidyalaxmi, a new central sector scheme 
in November 2024. Under the scheme, collateral-free and guarantor-free education loan is provided 

to a ll the students who get merit -based admission in top Quality Higher Education Institutions 
(QHEIs) and who desire to avail the education loan. Further, for students with annual family income 
up to ₹8 lakh, the scheme provides 3% interest subvention on loan s up to ₹10 lakh , during 
moratorium period i.e. course period plus one year . Each year up to one lakh fresh students not 
availing any other scholarship or interest subvention on education loan are eligible for this interest 
subvention benefit. An outlay of ₹ 3,600 crore has been made from 2024 -25 to 2030 -31, for 
providing 3% interest subvention benefit for up to 7 lakh fresh students during this period.  
 
Further, the Department of Higher Education is implementing the PM Uchchatar Shiksha Protsahan 
Yojna (PM -USP). Under Central Sector Interest Subsidy Scheme component of PM -USP full 
interest subsidy during the moratorium period on loan amount upto ₹10 lakh is provided for 
pursuing technical/professional courses in India. Students whose annual gro ss parental/ family 
income is up to ₹4.5 lakh are eligible under the scheme. PM-USP CSIS is also being administered 
through the PM-Vidyalaxmi portal and PM- Vidyalaxmi Digital Rupee Wallet.  
 
Since the launch of this scheme on 6 th November, 2024 till 27th July, 2026, 115,528 collateral-free 
and guarantor-free PM Vidyalaxmi education loans have been sanctioned. The amount sanctioned 
is ₹ 15, 994.59 crore. These are for course duration of upto 5 years. The yearly claims of interest 
subvention for a particular financial year are received in the next financial year.  Out of 16469 PM 
Vidyalaxmi education loan sanctioned from 6th November, 2024 to 31st March 2025, 5534 claims 
for interest subvention benefit pertaining to financial year 2024 -25 were received in the FY 2025-
26. As of July 22, 2026, there are 35,777 active Digital Rupee wallets under PM-Vidyalaxmi and 
PM-USP CSIS enabling disbursement of subsidies worth ₹57.66 crore.   
 
Under Credit Guarantee Fund Scheme for Education Loans (CGFSEL) of PM -USP, Central 
Government gives guarantee for the education loans availed by students without any collateral 
security and third -party guarantee for a maximum loan limit of ₹. 7.5 Lakh. The Fund provides 
guarantee cover to the extent of 75% of the amount in default through the National Credit Guarantee 
Trustee Company Ltd. (NCGTC). Government periodically reviews implementation of these 
schemes with participating banks to improve transparency and timely processing. Since the launch 
of the scheme in 2015 till 30th June, 2026, 1465102 credit guarantees for an amount of ₹ 59814.79 
crore have been issued.  
 
To ensure that timely and correct information is provided by Banks, CGFSEL notification dated 
16.09.2015 provides that every bank has to apply for guarantee cover in respect of education loans 
disbursed in a quarter, prior to expiry of the following quarter . Further, every education loan is to 
be linked with Aadhar number of the student.  

 
A dedicated online platform, the PM Vidyalaxmi portal https://pmvidyalaxmi.co.in has been 
developed, operational since 25 th February 2025, on which students can apply for the education 
loan, interest subvention and raise grievances. From 25th February 2025 till 25th July, 2026, a total 
of 34,066 grievances have been received, out of which 32,798 grievances have been resolved. 1268 
grievances are pending. Of these, 65% pending grievances have been filed in less than 30 days and 
72% of the remaining grievances are pending at 3 banks mainly. This Ministry regularly reviews 
the performance of the banks through the Portal . Department of Higher Education along with 
Department of Financial Services and Indian Bank’s Association (IBA) conducts regular meetings 
with participating banks, monitors the pendency, and follows up for timely disposal of applications 
and grievances.   
The Model Educational Loan Scheme of India Banks’ Association (IBA) guideline s provide that 
applications for educational loans received by the banks are to be disposed of in the normal course  
within a period of 15 days. At present turn around time ( TAT) of education loans is less than 15 
days.  
State-wise and year -wise number and amount of PM-Vidyalaxmi education loan sanctioned  and 
disbursed is at Annexure -I. District-wise, year -wise, number of category and gender  wise 
sanctioned education loan data for the State of Andhra Pradesh is at Annexure -II. State-wise and

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
DEPARTMENT OF HIGHER EDUCATION 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2385 
ANSWERED ON 03/08/2026 
 
Review of PhD Programmes in Universities 
 
2385. Shri Parshottambhai Rupala: 
 
Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the University Grants Commission (UGC) has initiated a comprehensive review of Ph.D. 
programmes in Central, State and private universities, if so, the details thereof, including the key 
findings and the corrective actions taken/proposed to be taken by the Government; 
 
(b) the measures implemented by UGC to improve the quality, relevance and integrity of Ph.D. 
research, including supervision norms, coursework rigor, plagiarism controls and outcome -based 
evaluation aligned with national priorities; 
 
(c) the reasons for not revoking Ph.D. degrees obtained through fraudulent means and not initiating 
criminal proceedings and whether stricter enforcement is under consideration, if so, the details 
thereof; and 
 
(d) whether UGC proposes a nati onal recognition or incentive framework for Ph.D. research 
delivering measurable national benefits? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(DR. SUKANTA MAJUMDAR) 
 
(a) to (d): The University Grants Commission (UGC) has notified the UGC (Minimum Standards and 
Procedures for Award of Ph.D. Degree) Regulations, 2022, which are applicable to all Universities 
established or incorporated under a Central Act, Provincial Act or State Act, Institutions Deemed to 
be Universities under Section 3 of the UGC Act, 1956, and degree -granting autonomous colleges 
permitted to offer Ph.D. programmes.  
As per the information received from the UGC, a Standing Committee was constituted by 
UGC on 20.04.2023 to suggest measures to control v iolations of UGC Regulations for award of 
Ph.D. Thereafter, an Expert Committee was also constituted to analyse the data of Ph.D. degrees 
awarded by the universities to extend help to the Standing Committee.  This Expert Committee has 
been entrusted with the task of examining/evaluating the data provided by the Universities in respect 
of the Ph.D. degrees awarded by them and give its recommendations whether these Universities 
awarded the Ph.D. degrees in accordance with the provisions stipulated in the UGC P h.D. 
Regulations 2009, 2016 and 2022.  The Standing Committee, after considering the report of the 
Expert Committee, gives its recommendations, which is subsequently placed before the UGC 
Commission for consideration and approval. 
UGC takes action against the Universities, who do not follow the UGC regulations. Till date, 
92 Universities have been examined/ reviewed to see whether they have been maintaining data and 
awarding Ph.D. as per UGC Regulations, out of which  5 universities  have been debarred from 
enrolling students in Ph.D. programme for the next 5 years . Ph.D programmes(s) offered by these 
universities, in the absence of UGC approval, shall not be treated as recognized/valid for the purpose 
of higher education and employment.

No. 2386 for August 3, 2026, Regarding ‘New Companies’. 
 
The Ministry of Corporate affairs (MCA) has undertaken specific initiatives and 
policies to strengthen the Ease of Doing Business, simplify company registration 
and the compliance framework in the corporate sector, such as: 
  I.    Amendments have been made in the Companies Act, 2013 (CA -13) in 2015 
& 2017 to facilitate ease of doing business and address concerns expressed by 
industry chambers & other stakeholders. 
 II.    Amendments have been made in CA-13 in 2019 and 2020 to de -criminalize 
technical & procedural violations and thus reduce the burden on criminal courts 
& National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT). They were also aimed at streamlining 
compliance requirements for Small Companies, One Person Companies, Start -
ups and Producer companies. 
 III.  Amendments have been made in the Limited Liability Partnership 
(Amendment) Act, 2021 to decriminalise technical & procedural violations. A 
new category of "Small LLP" was established for providing reduced compliance 
burden and lower fees to encourage formalization of small businesses. 
 IV.   Exemptions from various provisions of Companies Act to Private companies, 
Government Companies, Charitable companies, Nidhis and IFSC (GIFT city) 
companies have been provided through issuance of notifications under section 
462 of the CA-13 during 2015, 2017 and 2020. 
    V.  There is no fee for incorporation of company with authorized capital up to 
Rs.15.00 Lakh. 
 VI.   Direct listing of securities by Indian public companies in permissible 
foreign jurisdictions has been allowed. This is a boost for "Brand India" and 
increases attractiveness to growing technology sector, stimulates efficiency & 
growth, provides alternative source of capital and broadens investor base. 
VII.  The scope of fast -track merger was expanded in February 2021 to allow 
mergers of Start-ups with other Start-ups and with Small companies. The ambit 
has been further broadened in September 2025 to allow more classes of 
companies to choose this route. The rules have also been amended so that the 
"deemed approval" requirement is implemented more effectively for fast -track 
mergers. 

Page 5 of 5 
 
VIII. The Central Registration Centre (CRC) was operationalized in 2016 to 
provide speedy incorporation related services. An e -Form SPICe+ along with a 
linked form called AGILE PRO-S was introduced for providing different services 
at one place such as Name  Reservation, Incorporation, Allotment of PAN, TAN, 
DIN, EPFO Registration, ESIC Registration, GST number, opening of Bank 
Account etc. at the time of incorporation of company to start the business 
immediately. Similarly, new e -Form FiLLiP (Form for incorp oration of Limited 
Liability Partnership) was introduced for LLPs. 
 IX.     The LLP Incorporation Form called FiLLiP has also been integrated with 
Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT) to provide PAN/TAN at the   time of 
Incorporation of LLP itself. 
  
 X.     The Centre for Processing Accelerated Corporate Exit (C -PACE) was 
established in May 2023 enabling the stakeholders by providing a hassle -free 
filing, timely and process -bound striking off their companies' and LLPs' names 
from the Register. 
 XI.            The Central Processing Centre (CPC) was established in February 
2024 for centralized processing of 12 non-STP forms. 
XII.            The Companies (Adjudication of Penalties) Rules, 2014 have been 
amended in August 2024 pursuant to which it has been provided that the 
adjudication proceedings under section 454 of the Companies Act, 2013 shall 
take place in electronic mode only through the e-adjudication platform developed 
by the Ministry for this purpose. The platform provides for end -to-end digital 
process including online generation of notices, hearings, generation of 
adjudication orders and payments. This enhances trans parency and enables 
speeder adjudication. 
XIII.            The Ministry has, vide G.S.R. 880(E) dated 1st December, 2025, 
notified the Companies (Specification of definition details) Amendment Rules, 
2025, enhancing the thresholds for small companies. The paid -up capital 
criterion has been increased from "not more than Rs. 4 crores" to "not more than 
Rs. 10 crores" and turnover criterion has been increased from "not more than Rs. 
40 crores" to "not more than Rs. 100 crores". 
XIV.            The annual KYC requirement for directors in companies under rule 
12A of the Companies (Appointment & Qualification of Directors) Rules, 2014 
has been amended w.e.f. 31st March, 2026. Annual KYC requirement has been 
replaced with a simpler KYC intimation once in every three years.

(c) whether the Government has established administrative or legislative mechanisms to  ensure 
that teaching positions do not face backlogs or remain vacant in the future, if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(DR. SUKANTA MAJUMDAR) 
 
 
(a) to ( c) The Central Higher Education Institutions (CHEIs) under Ministry of Education 
including Central Universities (CUs), Indian Institutes of Technology ( IITs), Indian Institutes of 
Management (IIMs) are statutory autonomous organizations established under respective Central 
Acts of Parliament and governed by provisions of the Acts/Statutes/Ordinances/Regulations  etc. 
made thereunder. As autonomous institutions, faculty recruitment is done within the institutions 
itself, in accordance with their Acts and Regulations. The authority for recruitment to these posts 
vests with the respective Board of Governors/Executive Committee/Board of Management. 
 
Occurring of vacancies and filling thereof is a continuous process. The vacancies arise due to 
promotion, retirement, resignation, death, opening of new institutions, schemes or projects, and 
additional requirements on account of enhanced students’ strength and expansion of capacity in 
existing institutions.  

Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, in its Order dated 15.01.2026 in the matter of Amit Kumar & 
Others vs. Union of India & Others (Criminal Appeal No. 1425 of 2025), has, inte r alia, issued 
directions regarding the filling up of vacancies in the posts of Vice-Chancellors, Registrars, other 
key institutional/administrative positions, and faculty positions. 
In compliance with the aforesaid Order, the Ministry has forwarded the Or der to the Higher and 
Technical Education Departments of all States/UTs, Centrally Funded Higher Educational 
Institutions under the Ministry of Education, regulatory bodies such as University Grants 
Commission (UGC), All India Council for Technical Educati on (AICTE) for necessary 
compliance. 
In August, 2021, all CHEIs under Ministry of Education were requested to undertake special drive 
to fill backlog vacancies in their institutions in Mission Mode. The CHEIs undertook special 
recruitment drives to fill th e vacancies including of Scheduled Castes (SCs), Scheduled Tribes 
(STs) and Other Backward Classes (OBCs). In September 2022, Ministry of Education had also 
exhorted all the CHEIs to fill up the vacancies in Mission Mode. In October 2025, all the CHEIs 
have again been requested to fill up all the backlog vacancies in Mission Mode. From September 
2022, all CHEIs including Central Universities,  IITs and IIMs  have undertaken Mission Mode 
recruitment drive to fill the vacancies. Up to 23.05.2026 (i.e. the date of last Rozgar Mela), a total 
number of 32114 posts (3851 SC, 1643 ST, 6785 OBC, 1191 EWS) have been filled up by all 
CHEIs, including 18757 faculty positions (2315 SC, 910 ST, 3986 OBC, 568 EWS), in Mission 
Mode. 
 
In Centrally funded Higher Education Institutions, several measures have been taken to attract 
quality faculties which includes year-round open advertisements, recruitment through search-cum-
selection procedures, special recruitment drive, mission mode rec ruitment and invitation to 
alumni/scientists/faculty, etc. The faculty recruitment processes are carried out by the CHEIs by 
inviting applications in a transparent manner, as part of a multi-step and robust screening process. 
The Acts and Statutes of vario us institutions specify the composition of selection committees, 
authorities responsible for recruitment of various levels of faculty, provision of independent 
subject experts and Visitor’s nominees etc. so as to ensure transparency and academic rigour in 
recruitments. UGC has launched a common portal ‘CU -CHAYAN’ for faculty recruitment, 
making provision for listing of vacancies/ advertisements/ jobs across all Central Universities, thus 
making the entire recruitment process more transparent and accessible.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
DEPARTMENT OF SCHOOL EDUCATION & LITERACY 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO:- 2389 
ANSWERED ON-03/08/2026 
 
Waiver of Teacher Eligibility Test 
 
†2389. Shri Satpal Brahamchari: 
 Shri Jai Parkash: 
 
Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government is aware of the fact that many teachers appointed before the year 2010 were 
appointed as per the recruitment rules applicable at that time and mandatory passing of Teacher 
Eligibility Test (TET) was implemented later; 
(b) if so, whether the Government has held any consultation or review with the States regarding 
exemption from TET requirement or making special provisions for the said teachers; 
(c) if so, the main findings and decisions taken thereof; 
(d) whether the Government is considering removing the mandatory requirement of TET or providing 
an alternative arrangement to protect the interests of teachers appointed before the year 2010, keeping 
in view the National Education Policy (NEP) and the objectives of quality education; and 
(e) if so, the details thereof? 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(SHRI JAYANT CHAUDHARY) 
 
(a) to (e): Education is a subject in the Concurrent List of the Constitution and the recruitment, service 
conditions and deployment of teachers fall within the administrative domain of the respective State 
Governments and Union Territory Administrations.  
The Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, vide its judgment dated 01.09.2025, inter alia, held that the Teacher 
Eligibility Test (TET) is one of the minimum qualifications prescribed under Section 23 of the Right of 
Children to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act, 2009 , and is mandatory for appointment as a 
teacher in schools covered under the Act . The order of the Hon'ble Supreme Court may be accessed at 
the following link:  
https://api.sci.gov.in/supremecourt/2018/36466/36466_2018_9_1501_63764_Judgement_01-Sep-
2025.pdf 
Subsequently, while disposing of the review petitions in the matter, vide judgment dated 29.05.2026 the 
Hon'ble Supreme Court extended the timeline for acquisition of TET qualification from 31.08.2027 to 

31.08.2028. The judgment dated 29.05.2026  of the  Hon'ble Supreme Court may be accessed at the 
following link: 
https://api.sci.gov.in/supremecourt/2025/53434/53434_2025_7_1501_71637_Judgement_29-May-
2026.pdf 
The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the judgment dated 29.05.2026, has further observed that the respective 
appropriate Governments/authorities should endeavour to conduct the Teacher Eligibility Test (TET) 
periodically, preferably twice every year, with an interval of approximately six months between 
successive examinations, so as to afford eligible teache rs a reasonable opportunity to comply with the 
prescribed minimum qualification.

Retention Rates in School Education

Shri Saptagiri Sankar Ulaka: 
Adv Dean Kuriakose: 
Smt. Jyotsna Charandas Mahant: 
 
Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the details of Gross Enrolment Ratio (GER) at the primary, secondary and senior secondary levels since 
2018-19, year-wise and State/UT-wise including Chhattisgarh; 
(b) the percentage of students enrolled in Class I who successfully completed Class XII, since 2018 -19, 
year-wise and State/UT-wise; 
(c) the transition rate from Class 10 to Class 11 since 2018-19, year-wise, social-category and gender-wise, 
State/UT-wise including Left Wing Extremism (LWE) affected and tribal-majority districts like Bastar and 
Surguja of Chhattisgarh during the same period; 
(d) whether the Government has conducted any assessment regarding the primary factors contributing to 
dropouts and low transition rates among tribal girls at the secondary and senior secondary levels, if so, the 
details thereof, State/UT-wise including Chhattisgarh; and 
(e) the measures taken/proposed to be taken by the Government to improve retention and transition rates, 
establish residential hostels, and ensure continuous schooling among rural and marginalized communities 
especially in Chhattisgarh? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(SHRI JAYANT CHAUDHARY) 
 
(a): As per Unified District Information System for Education Plus (UDISE+),  State/UT wise including 
Chhattisgarh Gross Enrolment Ratio (GER) at the primary, secondary and senior secondary levels from the 
year 2018-19 to 2025-26 is at annexure-I. 
 
(b): As per UDISE+, State/UT wise retention rate at Higher Secondary level from the year 2019-20 to 2025-
26 is at annexure-II. 
 
(c): As per UDISE+, State/UT wise and gender-wise transition rate from Secondary to Higher Secondary 
(10 to 11) level from the year 2018-19 to 2025-26 is at annexure-III. 
 
(d): As per report titled ‘Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS)’ for the year 2023-24 released by Ministry 
of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI), the major reasons for the students who never 
attended the schools are to supplement household income, to attend domestic chores, etc. 
 

 
(e): Education is in the concurrent list of the Constitution and majority of the schools are under the domain 
of respective State and UT Governments.  The Central Government assist  States and UTs through the 
Centrally Sponsored Scheme of Samagra Shiksha and hot cooked meal provided from Balvatika to class 8 
under Pradhan Mantri Poshan Shakti Nirman (PM POSHAN) Yojna. Financial assistance/grant is also 
provided to the States and UTs including Chhattisgarh for various activities to reduce dropout and increase 
enrolment in Government schools, which include opening/strengthening of new schools up to Senior 
Secondary level, strengthening school infrastructure, setting up and up gradation and running of Kasturba 
Gandhi Balika Vidyalayas (KGBV) upto class 12, setting up of residential schools/hostels named Netaji 
Subhas Chandra Bose Avasiya Vidyalayas, hostels under Pradhan Mantri Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha 
Abhiyan (PM -JANMAN) and Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan (DAJGUA), transport 
allowance, undertaking enrolment drives, seasonal hostels/residential camps, provision of vocational 
education and ICT facilities in schools, providing free text books and free uniform, transport/escort facility, 
etc.

(b) the amount recovered from such written -off accounts during the same period, year -wise and

(c) the break-up of loans written off during the last five years, sector -wise (agriculture, industry, 
MSME, retail); and 
(d) the outstanding amount owed by wilful defaulters as on date and the number of such cases 
actually referred for criminal action, as distinct from those merely declared willful defaulters?

(SHRI PANKAJ CHAUDHARY)

Recognition of e-Sports 
 
2393.          SHRI ARUN BHARTI: 
                   SHRI RAJESH VERMA: 
                   SMT. SHAMBHAVI: 
 
Will the Minister of YOUTH AFFAIRS AND SPORTS be pleased to 
state: 
 
(a) whether the Government has prescribed the criteria, process and 
timeline for recognition of an e -sport under the National Sports 
Governance Act, 2025;  
  
(b) if so, the manner in which such recognition interfaces with 
registration with the Online Gaming Authority of India under the 
Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming Rules, 2 026 notified on 
22 April 2026; 
  
(c) the details of total number of e -sports titles and providers 
recognised or registered, as on date; 
  
(d) whether a coordination mechanism has been established between 
the Ministry of Youth Affair and Sports and the Ministry of Electronics 
and Information Technology for this purpose; and 
  
(e) if so, the details thereof ? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF YOUTH AFFAIRS AND SPORTS 
[DR. MANSUKH MANDAVIYA] 
  
(a) & (b): The National Sports Governance Act, 2025 has been 
enacted to provide for the development and promotion of sports, 

Page 2 of 2 
 
welfare measures for sportspersons, ethical practices based on 
basic universal principles of good governance, ethics and fair play of 
the Olympic and sports movement, the Olympic Charter, the 
Paralympic Charter, international best practices and established 
legal standards and to provide for the resolution of sports grievances 
and sports disputes in a unified, equitable and effective m anner and 
for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto. The select 
sections of the National Sports Governance Act, 2025 has already 
been notified on 31.12.2025 and 12.05.2026. Further, the National 
Sports Governance (National Sports Bodies) Rules,  2026 framed 
under the National Sports Governance Act, 2025 has been notified on 
12.01.2026. The said Rules lay down a statutory framework relating 
to governance standards, compliance requirements, ethical conduct, 
and institutional accountability within t he sports ecosystem. The 
Copies of the Act, the Notification and Rules are available on the 
website of the Ministry at the following link: 
https://yas.gov.in/en/sports/nsga-2025. Whereas the Promotion and 
Regulation of Online Gaming (PROG) Act, 2025 and th e rules made 
thereunder provide the statutory framework relating to online 
gaming, including registration of e -sports with the Online Gaming 
Authority of India (OGAI). 
  
(c)     At present, no e-sport has been registered under the Promotion 
and Regulation of Online Gaming Act, 2025. 
  
(d) & (e): Under the Government of India (Allocation of Business) 
Rules, 1961, matters relating to online gaming are allocated to the 
Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology, while e -Sports 
as part of multi -sports e vents are allocated to the Department of 
Sports. 
  
The Online Gaming Authority of India constituted under the PROG 
Act, 2025 as an attached office of the Ministry of Electronics and 
Information Technology and, inter -alia, has representation from the 
Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports in accordance with the 
applicable provisions.

TO BE ANSWERED ON MONDAY, AUGUST 03, 2026/SHRAV ANA 12, 1948 (SAKA) 
GST Rebates for Assistive Devices for Persons with Disabilities 
 2394. Shri Asaduddin Owaisi: 
 Will the Minister of FINANCE be pleased to state:  
(a) whether the Goods and Services Tax (GST) regime provides any benefits and 
exemptions for products related to assistive devices for persons with disabilities, if so, 
the details thereof;  
(b) the details of the tax exemptions and deductions for Persons with Disabilities 
(PWDs) to provide financial relief to persons with disabilities and their families in the 
new Income Tax regime; 
 (c) the details of the schemes to introduce financial incentives for private insurance 
companies to provide health insurance to persons with disabilities; and 
(d) the details of GST collection received on disability services and products by the GST 
Council during the last five years, State-wise and disability-wise? 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE 
(SHRI PANKAJ CHAUDHARY) 
 
(a): Yes, most specified assistive devices, rehabilitation aids and other goods for 
Persons with Disabilities (PWDs) attract a concessional GST rate of 5% (list enclosed 
as Annexure-I), while certain specified goods are exempt from GST. Further, certain 
services relating to rehabilitation, treatment and care of PWDs are also exempt from 
GST, subject to the prescribed conditions in the relevant notification. 
 
(b): The details of tax exemptions and deductions for PWDs under the new Income Tax 
regime are enclosed at Annexure-II. 
 
(c): The Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI) has not 
introduced any scheme providing ﬁnancial incentives to private insurance companies 
for oﬀering health insurance coverage to persons with disabilities. However, it has 
mandated all general and health insurers to oﬀer at least one health insurance product 
each for persons with disabilities, in accordance with the model product for persons 
with disabilities notiﬁed vide Circular No. IRDAI/HLT/ClR/MlSC/58/2/2023 dated 
27.02.2023. 
 
(d): The details of GST collection received on disability services and products, in the 
manner sought, is not maintained separately. 
 
 

ANNEXURE-I 
Refer to reply to part (a) of Lok Sabha Unstarred Question No. 2394 for answer on 03.08.2026 
• List of assistive devices and technologies used by PWDs attracting concessional GST rate of 5% 
(A) Orthopaedic appliances, such as crutches, surgical belts, and trusses; Splints and

(2) Equipment for  the mechanical or the computerized production of braille and 
recorded material  such as  braille computer terminals and displays, electronic

(3) Braille paper

(5) Aids for improving mobility of the blind such as electronic orientation and

(6) Technical aids  for education, rehabilitation,  vocational training  and

ANNEXURE-II 
Refer to reply to part (b) of Lok Sabha Unstarred Question No. 2394 for answer on 03.08.2026 
Details of tax exemptions and deductions under the new Income Tax regime 
The new tax regime under section 202 of the Income -tax Act, 2025 (the Act) is designed to 
provide substantial tax relief and simplified compliance through lower slab rates, higher 
standard deductions, and generous tax rebates. The general benefits available under the new 
tax regime, including to persons with disabilities, are as follows: 
1. Simplified Tax Slabs and Lower Rates 
Income Rate 
Up to ₹4,00,000 Nil 
₹4,00,001 to ₹8,00,000 5% 
₹8,00,001 to ₹12,00,000 10% 
₹12,00,001 to ₹16,00,000 15% 
₹16,00,001 to ₹20,00,000 20% 
₹20,00,001 to ₹24,00,000 25% 
Above ₹24,00,000 30% 
2. Tax-Free Income up to ₹12,00,000 via Enhanced Rebate 
Under Section 156(2), resident individuals opting for the new tax regime receive an 
exceptionally high tax rebate. Marginal relief is also provided if the income slightly exceeds 
₹12,00,000. 
3. Increased Standard Deduction for Salaried Taxpayers 
Salaried individuals under the new regime benefit from a higher standard deduction of ₹75,000 
(or the amount of salary, whichever is less). 
4. Higher Standard Deduction on Family Pension 
The deduction is one-third of the family pension received or ₹25,000, whichever is less. 
Benefits available under the new tax regime specifically for people with disabilities 
1. Exemption of Armed Forces Disability Pension (Schedule III, Sl. No. 38A): 
Disability pension received by a former member of the armed forces or paramilitary forces of 
the Union who was invalided out due to service -attributable or service -aggravated bodily 
disability is fully exempt from tax. 
2. Exclusion from Clubbing: 
Under the Act, a minor child’s income is clubbed with the income of the parent who earns 
more. However, if the minor child is suffering from a disability of the nature specified in 
Section 154, their income is excluded from clubbing and is assessed separat ely as per 
provisions under Section 99(1)(c)(iii).

KARNATAKA'S SHARE IN THE DIVISIBLE POOL OF CENTRAL TAXES 
 
2395. SHRI. E TUKARAM:     
Will the Minister of FINANCE be pleased to state:  
a) whether Karnataka's share in the divisible pool of Central taxes was reduced under the 15th Finance 
Commission as compared to the 14th Finance Commission and subsequently revised under the 16th 
Finance Commission, if so, the details thereof; 
b) the reasons for such reduction under the 15th Finance Commission and the factors considered while 
revising the share under the 16th Finance Commission; 
c) whether the Union Government has assessed the impact of these changes on Karnataka's finances and 
development expenditure, if so, the details thereof; and 
d) whether the Government proposes to review the criteria for horizontal tax devolution so as to ensure 
equitable distribution among States contributing significantly to the national economy and if so, the 
details thereof? 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE 
(SHRI PANKAJ CHAUDHARY) 
a) Karnataka’s share in divisible pool of Central taxes and duties under 15th FC was 3.647%. It was 
4.713% during the 14th FC and it is 4.131% as per 16th FC. 
  
b) Changes in share of divisible pool are on account of changes in indicators/criteria and their 
associated weights during the 15th Finance Commission. The 16th Finance Commission considered 
the following criteria which resulted in revision of the share of Karnataka.

One Year M.A. Course for FYUP 
 
†2398. Shri Sanjay Haribhau Jadhav: 
 Shri Arvind Ganpat Sawant: 
 Shri Sanjay Uttamrao Deshmukh: 
 
Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government is aware that the School of Open Learning (SOL), University of 
Delhi has not yet started the one year M.A. course for graduates of the Four Year 
Undergraduate Programme (FYUP) despite the regular department executing the same, if so, 
the reasons therefor; 
 
(b) whether the said situation is undermining the provisions of academic equity, flexibility 
and credit mobility under the NEP, 2020 and adversely affecting its effective implementation, 
if so, the details thereof; 
 
(c) whether the Government is aware that due to this said problem students of regular 
professional courses like L.L.B. are being deprived of the benefit of pursuing a one -year 
postgraduate course through the Open and Distance Learning (ODL) mode; 
 
(d) if so, the concrete and timebound remedial steps being taken by the Government, 
University Grants Commission (UGC) and Distance Education Bureau (DEB) to implement 
the one year M.A. programme at SOL for graduates of the FYUP during the current academic 
session; 
 
(e) whether the UGC and the DEB have issued or propose to issue any directions for 
commencing the one year M.A. programme in SOL during the current academic year or to 
make the necessary amendments to the entrance rules, if so, the details thereof; and 
 
(f) whether this anomaly is likely to discourage students from taking admission into the 
fourth year of the FYUP? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(DR. SUKANTA MAJUMDAR) 
 
(a) to (f): University of Delhi is a statutory autonomous organization established under an Act 
of Parliament and governed by the Delhi University Act, 1922 and the Statutes and the 
Ordinances made thereunder. It provides quality and af fordable education to the students 
from all over the country with its colleges including School of Open Learning (SOL) spread 

out all across the Delhi NCR region. The University has taken sincere steps to implement the 
National Education Policy 2020. The U niversity has informed that School of Open Learning 
has started the admission process for one year Master’s Degree Program under Open and 
Distance Learning (ODL) mode from Academic Session 2026 -27. The University Grants 
Commission (UGC) has also issued cir cular regarding offering One -year Postgraduate 
Programmes under Open and Distance Learning (ODL) in accordance with the National 
Education Policy, 2020. The UGC has further informed that as per regulation 2(z) of 
University Grants Commission (Open and Distance Learning Programmes and Online 
Programmes) Regulations, 2020, some programs including Law and their allied domains are 
excluded from the purview of Open and Distance Learning Mode and Online Mode in Higher 
Education.

INSTITUTION OF BUCKWHEAT FLOWER FESTIVAL IN LADAKH 
  
2400. SHRI MOHMAD HANEEFA: 
 
Will the Minister of TOURISM be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government has taken note of the success of Apricot 
Blossom Festivals in promoting tourism and local livelihoods in 
Ladakh; 
(b) whether the Government proposes to support the institution of a 
Buckwheat Flower Festival in Turtuk, Ladakh, on similar lines to 
promote agri -tourism, traditional agriculture, local cuisine, 
handicrafts and cultural heritage; 
(c) whether any financial or technical assistance is proposed for 
organising such festivals in collaboration with the UT 
Administration, local communities and Self-Help Groups; 
(d) whether financial assistance under the Swadesh Darshan Scheme 
(SDS), Challenge -Based Destination Development (CBDD) or any 
other tourism scheme can be extended for organising such a 
festival; and 
(e) the details of steps taken/being taken by the Government to 
promote crop -based tourism festivals in remote border areas of 
Ladakh to generate sustainable livelihoods for local communities? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF TOURISM      (SHRI GAJENDRA SINGH SHEKHAWAT) 
 
(a) to (e): The Union Territory of Ladakh organizes the Apricot Blossom 
and the Buckwheat Flower Festival to showcase the region's rich 
horticultural heritage, traditional cuisine, handicrafts, folk traditions 
and cultural heritage. The UT has informed that these fest ivals have 
contributed to increasing tourist arrivals, generating livelihood 
opportunities through local entrepreneurship, and promoting indigenous 

products, thereby supporting the socio -economic development of local 
communities. 
 
The Ministry of Tourism provides Central Financial Assistance 
(CFA) to State Governments and Union Territory Administrations under 
the Domestic Promotion and Publicity including Hospitality (DPPH) 
Scheme for organizing fairs, festivals and tourism -related events, 
subject to the scheme guidelines and availability of funds. No proposal 
has been received from the Union Territory of Ladakh seeking financial 
assistance for the Apricot Blossom Festival or the Buckwheat Flower 
Festival. 
 
Further, the Ministry under the Swadesh Darshan Scheme and 
Challenge-Based Destination Development (CBDD), provides Central 
Financial Assistance to States and Union Territories for the 
development of tourism infrastructure and visitor amenities at 
destinations. These schemes do not provide financial assistance 
towards organizing festivals or events.

(a)whether it is a fact that the Employees Provident Fund Organization 
(EPFO) has invited applications from exempted Provident Fund Trusts 
to regularize their status under provisions of the Finance Act, 2026, the 
Income Tax Act, 2005 and the Code on Social Security; 
(b)if so, the details thereof; 
(c)whether it is also a fact that the Amnesty Scheme, 2026, provides a 
onetime opportunity for the Trusts recognized under the Income Tax

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
DEPARTMENT OF HIGHER EDUCATION 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2402 
ANSWERED ON 03/08/2026 
 
Dropout Rates of SC/ST/OBC/EWS Students in HEIs 
 
†2402. Shri Dharmendra Yadav: 
 Shri Aditya Yadav: 
Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the number of Scheduled Caste (SC), Scheduled Tribe (ST), Other Backward Class 
(OBC) and Economically Weaker Section (EWS) students who voluntarily withdrew from 
or dropped out of the Central Higher Educational Institut ions like IITs, IIMs and Central 
Universities during the last five years, institution-wise and category-wise; 
(b) the major reasons identified in this regard along with the special measures taken by the 
Government to reduce these dropout rates; 
(c) the details of the unpublicized findings of Internal Committees assigned with the task of 
evaluating the socio -economic and institutional factors, such as campus alienation or 
financial stress driving these specific attrition rates; and  
(d) the concrete, measurable mandates imposed on these premier institutions to reform their 
academic counseling frameworks and financial-aid models to ensure equitable retention? 
         
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(DR. SUKANTA MAJUMDAR) 
(a) to (d):  In the Higher Education sector, students have multiple options and they choose 
and migrate from one course or programme to another. Students also move out after being 
offered placement/employment while pursuing higher studies. However, to increase Access 
in Higher Education, the Government has taken various steps like Financial Assistance and 
Scholarships like Pradhan Mantri Uchchatar Shiksha Protsahan (PM -USP) Scheme, fee 
waiver/reduction of disadvantaged groups, promote study loans like PM -Vidyalakshmi 
scheme, establishment of more institutes, student support system like Establishment of 
Counselling Cells, strengthening of Grievance Redressal Mechanism, providing Remedial 
Coaching, initiatives under online and digital learning (ODL) like SWAYAM, National 
Digital Library (NDL) and e -PG Pathshala. Further, in light of NEP 2020, a slew of 
initiatives for academic reforms have been undertaken like Multiple Entry and Exit Options, 
Academic Bank of Credits (ABC) etc. 
To address the issue of equity and inclusion in the education, Government has taken 
multipronged approach and initiatives. UGC (Promotion of Equity in Higher Educational 
Institutions) Regulations, 2012 have been notified, which is applicable to all the HEIs under 
its purview. It provides for HEIs to take measures to safeguard the interests of the students 

without any prejudice to their caste, creed, religion, language, ethnicity, gender and 
disability. It inter alia,  stipulates setting up of Counselling Cen tres with professionally 
trained counsellors to provide services to students, research scholars and faculty including 
non-teaching staff. 
In order to proactively address any issues of SC / ST students, Institutes have set up 
mechanisms such as SC / ST stud ents’ cells, Equal Opportunity Cell, Student Grievance 
Cell, Student Grievance Committee, Student Social Club, Liaison officers, Liaison 
Committee etc. Further, University Grants Commission (UGC) has issued instructions from 
time to time for promoting equity and fraternity amongst students. 
UGC also issued Guidelines on 13.04.2023  for promoting physical fitness and sports 
activities for students; creating safeguards against academic pressure, peer pressure, 
behavioral issues, stress, career concerns, depres sion and other issues on the mental health 
of students; to teach positive thinking & emotions in the student community; and to promote 
a positive and supportive network for students. 
Further, UGC had also notified UGC Regulations on curbing the menace of R agging in 
Higher Educational Institutions, 2009 and amended it in 2016, and issued circulars for strict 
compliance of the regulations.  
 
To ensure a safe campus environment, UGC has launched an extensive anti-ragging outreach 
initiative across all of its official social media channels, including X (Twitter), Instagram, 
Facebook, LinkedIn, WhatsApp, and YouTube. These campaigns feature short videos, 
banners, and other creatives disseminated in 21 languages to ensure wide accessibility and 
engagement.  
 
A nationwide toll free 24x7 anti ragging helpline 1800 -180-5522 in 12 languages is in 
operation to offer timely and confidential assistance to students experiencing distress related 
to ragging, harassment, or emotional vulnerability.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
DEPARTMENT OF HIGHER EDUCATION 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO- 2406 
ANSWERED ON - 03/08/2026 
 
Establishment of Technical Education Institutions in Andhra Pradesh 
 
2406.    Shri Bastipati Nagaraju: 
 
Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state:  
 
(a) the details of the total number of technical education institutions established across the 
country, State-wise and district-wise, especially in Andhra Pradesh; 
(b) whether the Government has any plans to establish new technical education institutions, 
particularly in underserved regions of Andhra Pradesh, if so, the details thereof and if not, the 
reasons therefor; 
(c) the details of the funds allocated and released by the Government during the last five years 
for the establishment of technical education institutions, year-wise and State-wise; 
(d) whether the Government has taken any steps to improve the existing infrastructure of 
technical education institutions, including laboratories, digital classrooms, etc.; 
(e) if so, the details thereof along with the funds allocated and released in this regard, Statewise 
and year-wise; and 
(f) whether the Government plans to introduce new technical courses, skill-based modules and 
specialised workshops in emerging areas such as Artificial Intelligence (AI), robotics, data 
science and green technologies in such institutions and if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(DR. SUKANTA MAJUMDAR) 
 
(a) to (f): The All India Council for Technical Education (AICTE), a statutory body under the 
Ministry of Education, grants approval for conducting courses in Technical Education at 
diploma, undergraduate and post graduate levels to Technical Institutions, Institutions deemed 
to be Universities and standalone institutions in accordance with the provisions of the AICTE 
Act, 1987 and rules & regulations made thereafter. Approval is granted to eligible applicant 
institutions upon fulfilment of the prescribed norms and standards. The State/UT-wise details 
of AICTE-approved technical institutions, including in Andhra Pradesh, are at Annexure-I, 
and district-wise details of AICTE-approved technical institutions in the State of Andhra 

Pradesh are at Annexure-II. At present a total of 891 AICTE approved technical institutions 
are offering courses in the State of Andhra Pradesh.  
AICTE has undertaken several initiatives to strengthen the quality of technical education and 
institutional infrastructure through its regulatory framework. The Approval Process Handbook 
prescribes mandatory requirements relating to infrastructure, laboratories, instructional 
facilities, ICT-enabled classrooms, libraries, innovation facilities and other academic resources 
for AICTE-approved HEIs.  
To upgrade the higher education curricula, the All-India Council for Technical Education 
(AICTE) has revised its Model Curricula with inputs from industry experts by integrating 
Artificial Intelligence (AI), Data Science (DS), Machine Learning (ML), Cyber Security, 
Robotics, Quantum Computing, and other emerging technologies across technical disciplines. 
AICTE also supports the IDEA Labs & Modernization and Removal of Obsolescence 
(MODROBS), Industry-supported laboratories/ Centres of Excellence (CoEs) through MoU 
Partners under CSR initiatives to strengthen the teaching-learning process and innovation 
ecosystem.   
Further, AICTE undertakes regular consultations with industry, professional bodies, academia, 
and other stakeholders to ensure that technical education remains relevant, competency-based, 
multidisciplinary, and aligned with evolving workforce requirements keeping in line with the 
objectives of NEP.  
University Grants Commission (UGC) has notified the Curriculum and Credit Framework for 
Undergraduate Programmes and all HEIs have been asked to adopt the framework. The 
framework includes value-added courses such as digital and technological solutions in cutting-
edge areas that are fast gaining prominence like Artificial Intelligence (AI), 3-D printing, big 
data analysis, machine learning, drone technologies, and Deep learning etc., for enhancing the 
employability of the youth.  
Further UGC has initiated several summits, workshops, seminars in order to create awareness 
in emerging areas including, robotics, AI, machine learning etc such as 'Virtual Summit on 
Artificial Intelligence – Responsible AI for Social Empowerment (RAISE 2020), 'National 
Programme on Artificial Intelligence (NPAI)' to build momentum around skilling in Artificial 
Intelligence (AI). 
For strengthening infrastructure, the Government of India provides funds to State government 
under the Rashtriya Uchchatar Shiksha Abhiyan (RUSA) / Pradhan Mantri Uchchatar Shiksha 
Abhiyan (PM-USHA). Since the inception of this Scheme, in Andhra Pradesh a total of 167 
units have been approved with central support of Rs. 736.06 Crore under various components 

like creation of Model Degree Colleges and other infrastructure improvements. Further the 
States/UTs wise release of funds in financial year 2025-26 are at Annexure-III 
Government of India has established several Centrally Funded Institutions (CFIs)  in the State 
of Andhra Pradesh such as IIT Tirupati, IIM Vishakhapatnam, IISER Tirupati, IIIT Kurnool, 
NIT Andhra Pradesh, Central University Andhra Pradesh, Central Tribal University, Andhra 
Pradesh and National Sanskrit University, Tirupati (elevated) for providing quality education 
for the students.

PUBLIC DEBT AND FISCAL SUSTAINABILITY OF ANDHRA PRADESH 
 
2408.  Shri Y S Avinash Reddy  
Shri P V Midhun Reddy 
Will the Minister of Finance be pleased to state: 
(a) the total public debt of Andhra Pradesh in the Financial years 2024-25 and 2025-26 
including off-budget borrowings through State corporations and special purpose vehicles and 
the current debt-to-Gross State Domestic Product (GSDP) ratio of the State; 
(b) whether the Union Government has assessed the impact of Andhra Pradesh’s fiscal 
deficit of 4.6 per cent of GSDP in FY 2025-26 which significantly exceeds the limit 
prescribed by the 16th Finance Commission on the State’s interest payment burden and long-
term fiscal sustainability, if so, the details thereof; and 
(c) whether the Union Government has issued any corrective measures or advisory 
guidance to the Government of Andhra Pradesh to arrest the rising debt trajectory and 
safeguard essential public services and welfare expenditure in the State and if so, the details 
thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE 
(SHRI PANKAJ CHAUDHARY) 
 
(a) As per the information provided by the State Government of Andhra Pradesh for 
determination of borrowing ceiling under Article 293(3) of the Constitution of India, the 
details regarding total public debt of Andhra Pradesh during Financial year (FY) 2024-25 and 
2025-26 including off-budget borrowings through State corporations and special purpose 
vehicles is given at Annexure-I.As per the Reserve Bank of India’s report titled ‘State 
Finances: A Study of Budgets 2025-26’, the current debt-to-Gross State Domestic Product 
(GSDP) ratio of the State Government of Andhra Pradesh is 35.5 percent during FY 2024-25 
(Revised Estimates)and 35.4 percent during FY 2025-26 (Budget Estimates). 
  

(b) and (c) All States including Andhra Pradesh have enacted their Fiscal Responsibility and 
Budget Management (FRBM) Act which makes the State Government responsible to ensure 
prudence in fiscal management and fiscal stability by progressive elimination of revenue 
deficit, reduction in fiscal deficit, prudent debt management consistent with fiscal 
sustainability and greater transparency in fiscal operations of the government. Compliance to 
the State FRBM Act is monitored by the respective State Legislatures. 
Department of Expenditure, Ministry of Finance, usually considers the fiscal limits as 
per the accepted recommendations of the Finance Commission while granting consent for 
borrowings by States under Article 293(3) of the Constitution of India. Adjustments for the 
over-borrowing by States during previous year, if any, are made in the borrowing ceiling of 
subsequent year. To prevent circumvention of debt limits and promote transparency in 
reporting fiscal deficit, from the financial year 2021-22 onwards, the off-budget borrowings 
(OBBs) raised by States through the States Owned Entities are also treated as borrowings of 
the State Governments while granting consent for borrowing under Article 293(3) of the 
Constitution of India.

up to Rs. 15 lakh or with up to 20 members where no share capital is applicable.

streamlining compliance requirements for Small Companies, One Person

"Small LLP" was established for providing reduced compliance burden and lower 
fees to encourage formalization of small businesses.

of Start-ups with other Start -ups and with Small companies. The ambit has been

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF EDUCATION  
DEPARTMENT OF SCHOOL EDUCATION AND LITERACY 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO - 2410 
ANSWERED ON – 03/08/2026 
 
 
Status of Student-Teacher Ratio under Samagra Shiksha in Mainpuri 
 
†2410. Smt. Dimple Yadav: 
 
Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state: 
(a) the current status of the student -teacher ratio, subject -wise teacher vacancies of the 
teachers and the number of schools with single-teacher in Mainpuri under Samagra Shiksha; 
(b) the action taken by  the Central Government on proposals related to recruitment, 
redeployment or rationalization of teachers sent by the State Government of Uttar Pradesh 
since the year 2022; 
(c)   whether the Government has taken cognizance of the shortage of teachers or any deviation 
from norms prescribed in this regard in Mainpuri if so, the details thereof; and 
(d)   the details of steps taken by the Central Government to ensure the availability of teachers 
in accordance with prescribed norms? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(SHRI JAYANT CHAUDHARY) 
 
(a) to (d): Education being a subject in the Concurrent List of the Constitution, the 
majority of schools in the country are under the administrative control of the respective State 
Governments and Union Territory Administrations. Accordingly, the recruitment, service 
conditions and deployment of teachers fall within the administrative domain of the concerned 
States/UTs. 
 
  Teacher vacancies arise from time to time due to factors such as retirement, 
resignation, creation of new posts, rationalisation of teacher deployment and changes in 
enrolment. The data relating to sanctioned strength, vacant teaching posts is maintained by 
the respective State Governments and Union Territory Administrations.  
 
The Central Government periodically advises States/UTs to fill vacant posts through 
transparent and merit -based recruitment processes, including through autonomous teacher 
recruitment boards or similar mechanisms. The progress of recruitment is regularly reviewed 
through meetings and advisories, with emphasis on competitive selection, consistency and 
technology-based teacher requirement planning and forecasting.   

Further, the Central Government provides financial assistance to States/UTs under 
Samagra Shiksha to ma intain appropriate Pupil -Teacher Ratio (PTR) at various levels of 
schooling in accordance with the norms prescribed under the Right of Children to Free and 
Compulsory Education (RTE) Act, 2009.  
 
            Para 2.3 of the National Education Policy (NEP), 2020 emphasises maintaining a PTR 
of under 30:1 in each school and under 25:1 in areas with a high proportion of socio -
economically disadvantaged students.  
 
As informed by the state of Uttar Pradesh, the pupil-teacher ratio (PTR) in government 
primary, upper primary and secondary level in Mainpuri district, is 14, 18 and 20.5 which is 
within the norms envisaged under NEP 2020. The number of Primary Schools wit h single 
teacher in the district of Mainpuri is 40, the number of Upper Primary Schools with single 
teacher is 15 and the number of secondary schools with single teacher is zero.

2414. Shri Saptagiri Sankar Ulaka: 
          Shri Brijendra Singh Ola: 
          Shri Ramasahayam Raghuram Reddy: 
          Dr. Rajkumar Sangwan: 
 
Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether it is a fact that the Government has allocated budget through various schemes to promote 
digital education in school education in the line with the National Education Policy, 2020 since the year 
2018-19, if so, the details of the allocation and expenditure made in this regard, year-wise; 
(b) the total number of operational schools and the number of schools having acces s to computers, 
internet connectivity, smart classrooms and other digital learning infrastructure in schools functioning 
in rural and urban areas, State/UT-wise including Uttar Pradesh; 
(c) the number of teachers trained in digital pedagogy/digital teachin g methodology and use of 
technology since 2018-19 as on date, State/UT-wise and year-wise; 
(d) whether the Government has taken additional steps or is aware of the existing digital divide in access 
to digital devices and internet connectivity/access among school students, particularly in rural and 
remote areas, if so, the actions taken to address the divide; and 
(e) whether the Government has conducted any assessment of the impact of digital education such PM 
e-Vidya, DIKSHA and other digital education initiatives on learning outcomes and if so, the details of 
the findings and future action plan in this regard? 
ANSWER 
                                                                              
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(SHRI JAYANT CHAUDHARY) 
(a): The Government has been promoting digital education in school education through various 
initiatives under Samagra Shiksha, in alignment with the objectives of the National Education Policy 
(NEP), 2020. Financial assistance is provided to States  and Union Territories (UTs) under Samagra 
Shiksha for ICT infrastructure, including ICT Labs and Smart Classrooms, based on their Annual Work 
Plan & Budget (AWP&B) approved by the Project Approval Board (PAB). In addition, digital 
education initiatives su ch as DIKSHA and PM eVidya are implemented by the Ministry to provide 
equitable access to quality digital learning resources. 
The year-wise details of budget approved and expenditure under Samagra Shiksha for ICT Labs, Smart 
Classrooms and digital education initiatives since FY2018-19 are provided:
